bandDescriptors.minimal: A probability density function integrates to 1 over its domain — that equation gives k. For (b), integrate the same function from 0 to 1, in radians.

writtenQuestions.q:
A landscape gardener wants to build a garden bed in the shape of a rectangle attached to a quarter-circle. Let x and y be the dimensions of the rectangle in metres, as shown in the diagram.The garden bed is required to have an area of 36 m² and to have a perimeter which is as small as possible. Let P metres be the perimeter of the garden bed.

(a) Show that P = 2x + 72/x. (3 marks)

(b) Find the smallest possible perimeter of the garden bed, showing why this is the minimum perimeter. (4 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The quarter-circle has radius x, so
Area = xy + ¼πx² = 36, giving y = 36/x − πx/4.
The boundary is: the left side x, the top y, the quarter-circle arc ¼(2πx) = πx/2, and the bottom y + x.
P = x + y + πx/2 + y + x = 2x + 2y + πx/2.
Substituting y: P = 2x + 2(36/x − πx/4) + πx/2
= 2x + 72/x − πx/2 + πx/2
= 2x + 72/x.

(b) dP/dx = 2 − 72/x².
Setting dP/dx = 0: 2 = 72/x², so x² = 36 and x = 6 (x > 0).
d²P/dx² = 144/x³, which is positive at x = 6, so this is a minimum.
P = 2(6) + 72/6 = 12 + 12 = 24 metres.

bandDescriptors.full: P = 2x + 72/x derived correctly, then x = 6 from dP/dx = 0 and a minimum perimeter of 24 m justified by the positive second derivative.
bandDescriptors.partial: The perimeter is minimised correctly but the derivation in (a) is incomplete, or the minimum is not justified.
bandDescriptors.minimal: In (a) the πx terms cancel — the bottom edge is y + x, not y. In (b), solve dP/dx = 0 and then test the second derivative to show it is a minimum, not just a stationary point.

writtenQuestions.q:
Tina inherits $60 000 and invests it in an account earning interest at a rate of 0.5% per month. Each month, immediately after the interest has been paid, Tina withdraws $800.

The amount in the account immediately after the nth withdrawal can be determined using the recurrence relation An = An−1(1.005) − 800, where n = 1, 2, 3, … and A0 = 60 000.

(a) Use the recurrence relation to find the amount of money in the account immediately after the third withdrawal. (2 marks)

(b) Calculate the amount of interest earned in the first three months. (2 marks)

(c) Calculate the amount of money in the account immediately after the 94th withdrawal. (3 marks)

bandDescriptors.full: All three amounts correct — $58 492.49 after the third withdrawal, $892.49 of interest, and $187.85 after the 94th — with a closed form used for (c).
bandDescriptors.partial: Parts (a) and (b) correct, but (c) is wrong or attempted by iterating rather than by a closed form.
bandDescriptors.minimal: In (b), interest each month is 0.5% of that month's opening balance. For (c), expand the recurrence into a geometric series: Aₙ = 160 000 − 100 000(1.005)ⁿ.

writtenQuestions.q:
A cricket is an insect. The male cricket produces a chirping sound.

A scientist wants to explore the relationship between the temperature in degrees Celsius and the number of cricket chirps heard in a 15-second time interval.

Once a day for 20 days, the scientist collects data. Based on the 20 data points, the scientist provides the information below.

• A box-plot of the temperature data is shown.• The mean temperature in the dataset is 0.525°C below the median temperature in the dataset.
• A total of 684 chirps was counted when collecting the 20 data points.

The scientist fits a least-squares regression line using the data (x, y), where x is the temperature in degrees Celsius and y is the number of chirps heard in a 15-second time interval. The equation of this line is y = −10.6063 + bx, where b is the slope of the regression line.

The least-squares regression line passes through the point (x̄, ȳ) where x̄ is the sample mean of the temperature data and ȳ is the sample mean of the chirp data.

Calculate the number of chirps expected in a 15-second interval when the temperature is 19° Celsius. Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.
writtenQuestions.answer:
From the box-plot, the median temperature is 22°C.
So the mean is x̄ = 22 − 0.525 = 21.475°C.
The mean number of chirps is ȳ = 684/20 = 34.2.
The regression line passes through (21.475, 34.2):
34.2 = −10.6063 + b(21.475)
b = 44.8063/21.475 = 2.0864.
So y = −10.6063 + 2.0864x.
At x = 19: y = −10.6063 + 2.0864(19) = 29.04
≈ 29 chirps.

bandDescriptors.full: 29 chirps — median 22°C read from the box-plot, mean 21.475°C, ȳ = 34.2, slope 2.0864, then substitution of x = 19.
bandDescriptors.partial: The slope is found correctly but the final substitution is wrong, or the mean temperature is taken as the median.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Three numbers are needed before the slope: the median from the box-plot (22), the mean temperature (22 − 0.525) and the mean chirp count (684/20). The line passes through (x̄, ȳ).

writtenQuestions.q:
In a particular country, the hourly rate of pay for adults who work is normally distributed with a mean of $25 and a standard deviation of $5.

(a) Two adults who both work are chosen at random. Find the probability that at least one of them earns between $15 and $30 per hour. (3 marks)

(b) The number of adults who work is equal to three times the number of adults who do not work. One adult is chosen at random. Find the probability that the chosen adult works and earns more than $25 per hour. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) $15 is z = (15 − 25)/5 = −2 and $30 is z = (30 − 25)/5 = 1.
Using the empirical rule, P(−2 < z < 1) = 0.95/2 + 0.68/2 = 0.475 + 0.34 = 0.815.
P(neither of the two) = (1 − 0.815)² = 0.185² = 0.034225.
P(at least one) = 1 − 0.034225 = 0.9658.

(b) If w adults do not work, then 3w work, out of 4w in total, so P(works) = 3/4.
$25 is the mean, so P(earns more than $25 | works) = 0.5.
P(works and earns more than $25) = (3/4)(1/2) = 3/8 = 0.375.

bandDescriptors.full: Both parts correct — 0.9658 via the complement of 'neither', and 3/8 from P(works) = 3/4 multiplied by the half of the distribution above the mean.
bandDescriptors.partial: The 0.815 region is found correctly but 'at least one' is not handled by the complement, or (b) uses the wrong proportion of workers.
bandDescriptors.minimal: In (a), z = −2 and z = 1, and 'at least one' is easiest as 1 − P(neither). In (b), three times as many work as do not, so 3 in every 4 adults work; $25 is the mean, so exactly half of those earn more.

writtenQuestions.q:
The diagram shows the graph of y = c ln x, c > 0.(a) Show that the equation of the tangent to y = c ln x at x = p, where p > 0, is y = (c/p)x − c + c ln p. (2 marks)

(b) Find the value of c such that the tangent from part (a) has a gradient of 1 and passes through the origin. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) y = c ln x, so dy/dx = c/x.
At x = p the gradient is c/p and the point of contact is (p, c ln p).
Point-gradient form: y − c ln p = (c/p)(x − p)
y = (c/p)x − (c/p)(p) + c ln p
y = (c/p)x − c + c ln p.

(b) Gradient 1 means c/p = 1, so p = c.
Through the origin means (0, 0) satisfies the tangent:
0 = 0 − c + c ln p, so c ln p = c.
Since c > 0, ln p = 1 and p = e.
Therefore c = p = e.

bandDescriptors.full: Tangent derived correctly from dy/dx = c/x at the point (p, c ln p), then c = e found from the two conditions c/p = 1 and c ln p = c.
bandDescriptors.partial: The tangent equation is correct but the two conditions in (b) are not combined to reach c = e.
bandDescriptors.minimal: In (a) use the point (p, c ln p) with gradient c/p. In (b) the two conditions give p = c and ln p = 1 — solve them together.

writtenQuestions.q:
The diagram shows two parabolas y = 4x − x² and y = ax², where a > 0. The two parabolas intersect at the origin, O, and at A.(a) Show that the x-coordinate of A is 4/(a + 1). (2 marks)

(b) Find the value of a such that the shaded area is 16/3. (4 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) At an intersection the y-values are equal:
4x − x² = ax²
4x = ax² + x² = (a + 1)x²
x[(a + 1)x − 4] = 0
So x = 0 (the origin) or x = 4/(a + 1), which is the x-coordinate of A.

(b) Let k = 4/(a + 1). The shaded area is the region between the curves from 0 to k:
Area = ∫₀^k [(4x − x²) − ax²] dx = ∫₀^k [4x − (a + 1)x²] dx
= [2x² − (a + 1)x³/3]₀^k
= 2k² − (a + 1)k³/3.
Substituting k = 4/(a + 1):
= 32/(a + 1)² − 64/[3(a + 1)²]
= 32/[3(a + 1)²].
Set equal to 16/3: 32/[3(a + 1)²] = 16/3
(a + 1)² = 2, so a + 1 = √2 (positive since a > 0)
a = √2 − 1.

bandDescriptors.full: Intersection x = 4/(a + 1) established, the area between the curves integrated to 32/[3(a + 1)²], and a = √2 − 1 obtained.
bandDescriptors.partial: The area integral is set up correctly as upper curve minus lower curve, but the algebra does not reach a = √2 − 1.
bandDescriptors.minimal: In (a), equate the two expressions and factor out x. In (b), integrate (4x − x²) − ax² from 0 to the x-coordinate of A, then solve for a.

writtenQuestions.q:
The population of mice on an isolated island can be modelled by the function m(t) = a sin((π/26)t) + b, where t is the time in weeks and 0 ≤ t ≤ 52. The population of mice reaches a maximum of 35 000 when t = 13 and a minimum of 5000 when t = 39. The graph of m(t) is shown.(a) What are the values of a and b? (2 marks)

(b) On the same island, the population of cats can be modelled by the function c(t) = −80 cos((π/26)(t − 10)) + 120. Consider the graph of m(t) and the graph of c(t). Find the values of t, 0 ≤ t ≤ 52, for which both populations are increasing. (3 marks)

(c) Find the rate of change of the mice population when the cat population reaches a maximum. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The amplitude is half the range: a = (35 000 − 5000)/2 = 15 000.
The centre is the mean of the extremes: b = (35 000 + 5000)/2 = 20 000.

(b) m′(t) = 15 000(π/26) cos((π/26)t), which is positive when cos((π/26)t) > 0,
i.e. for 0 ≤ t < 13 and 39 < t ≤ 52.
c′(t) = 80(π/26) sin((π/26)(t − 10)), which is positive when sin((π/26)(t − 10)) > 0,
i.e. when 0 < (π/26)(t − 10) < π, giving 10 < t < 36.
Both increase on the overlap: 10 < t < 13.
(The interval 39 < t ≤ 52 does not overlap 10 < t < 36.)

(c) c(t) is greatest when cos((π/26)(t − 10)) = −1, i.e. (π/26)(t − 10) = π, so t = 36.
m′(36) = 15 000(π/26) cos(36π/26)
= 1812.4 × (−0.3546)
≈ −643.
The mice population is falling at about 643 mice per week.

bandDescriptors.full: a = 15 000 and b = 20 000; both populations increasing only on 10 < t < 13; and a rate of about −643 mice per week at t = 36.
bandDescriptors.partial: The amplitude and centre are correct and one derivative is analysed correctly, but the overlap or the final rate is wrong.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The amplitude is half the difference of the maximum and minimum, and b is their average. For (b), solve m′(t) > 0 and c′(t) > 0 separately and intersect. The cat population peaks where the cosine equals −1.

writtenQuestions.q: Solve x + (x − 1)/2 = 9.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Multiply every term by 2 to clear the fraction:
2x + (x − 1) = 18
3x − 1 = 18
3x = 19
x = 19/3 (that is, 6⅓)

Check: 19/3 + (19/3 − 1)/2 = 19/3 + (16/3)/2 = 19/3 + 8/3 = 27/3 = 9. ✓

bandDescriptors.partial: The fraction is cleared correctly to reach 3x − 1 = 18 or 3x = 19, but the final value is wrong or left unsimplified.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Multiply both sides by 2 first so the fraction disappears, then collect the x terms.

writtenQuestions.q:
A right-angled triangle XYZ is cut out from a semicircle with centre O. The length of the diameter XZ is 16 cm and ∠YXZ = 30°, as shown on the diagram.



(a) Find the length of XY in centimetres, correct to two decimal places. (2 marks)

(b) Hence, find the area of the shaded region in square centimetres, correct to one decimal place. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The angle in a semicircle is a right angle, so ∠XYZ = 90° and XYZ is right-angled at Y with hypotenuse XZ = 16 cm.

cos 30° = XY / XZ
XY = 16 cos 30° = 16 × (√3/2) = 8√3 = 13.8564…
XY = 13.86 cm (2 d.p.)

(b) The shaded region is the semicircle with the triangle removed.

Semicircle: radius 8, area = ½π(8)² = 32π = 100.5309… cm²

Triangle: the other side is YZ = 16 sin 30° = 8 cm, and the right angle is between XY and YZ, so
area = ½ × 8√3 × 8 = 32√3 = 55.4256… cm²

Shaded area = 100.5309 − 55.4256 = 45.1053…
Shaded area = 45.1 cm² (1 d.p.)

bandDescriptors.full: XY = 13.86 cm and the shaded area is 45.1 cm², found as semicircle minus triangle.
bandDescriptors.partial: XY is correct, or the method (semicircle − triangle) is correct but an area is miscalculated or the triangle's second side is wrong.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The angle in a semicircle is 90°, so XZ is the hypotenuse. For the shading, subtract the triangle's area from the semicircle's area.

writtenQuestions.q: Find the exact gradient of the tangent to the curve y = x tan x at the point where x = π/3.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Differentiate using the product rule, with u = x and v = tan x:
dy/dx = (1)(tan x) + (x)(sec²x) = tan x + x sec²x

At x = π/3:
tan(π/3) = √3
cos(π/3) = ½, so sec(π/3) = 2 and sec²(π/3) = 4

dy/dx = √3 + (π/3)(4) = √3 + 4π/3

bandDescriptors.full: The gradient is √3 + 4π/3.
bandDescriptors.partial: The product rule is applied correctly to give tan x + x sec²x, but the exact values at π/3 are wrong or the answer is left as a decimal.
bandDescriptors.minimal: x tan x is a product, so differentiate with the product rule. The derivative of tan x is sec²x, and sec(π/3) = 1 ÷ cos(π/3).

writtenQuestions.q:
The first term of an arithmetic sequence is 5. The sum of the first 43 terms is 2021.

What is the common difference of the sequence?

bandDescriptors.partial: The correct sum formula is set up with a = 5 and n = 43, but the equation is solved incorrectly.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Substitute a = 5, n = 43 and Sₙ = 2021 into Sₙ = (n/2)[2a + (n − 1)d] and solve for d.

writtenQuestions.q: Evaluate ∫−20 √(2x + 4) dx.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Write the integrand as a power: √(2x + 4) = (2x + 4)^(1/2).

Integrating (ax + b)ⁿ divides by a and raises the power by one:
∫ (2x + 4)^(1/2) dx = (2x + 4)^(3/2) ÷ (3/2) ÷ 2 = (1/3)(2x + 4)^(3/2)

Evaluate between x = −2 and x = 0:
= (1/3)(4)^(3/2) − (1/3)(0)^(3/2)
= (1/3)(8) − 0
= 8/3

bandDescriptors.full: The integral equals 8/3.
bandDescriptors.partial: The primitive (1/3)(2x + 4)^(3/2) is found but the limits are substituted incorrectly, or the division by the coefficient of x is omitted.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Rewrite the surd as (2x + 4)^(1/2), then integrate a linear-in-x power: raise the index by one, divide by the new index, and divide again by the coefficient of x.

writtenQuestions.q: For what values of x is f(x) = x² − 2x³ increasing?
writtenQuestions.answer:
A function is increasing where its derivative is positive.

f′(x) = 2x − 6x²
     = 2x(1 − 3x)

Solve 2x(1 − 3x) > 0. The roots are x = 0 and x = 1/3, and the parabola −6x² + 2x opens downwards, so the expression is positive between the roots.

0 < x < 1/3

bandDescriptors.full: f(x) is increasing for 0 < x < 1/3.
bandDescriptors.partial: The derivative is correct and set greater than zero, but the inequality is solved the wrong way round (giving x < 0 or x > 1/3) or only the roots are stated.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Increasing means f′(x) > 0. Differentiate, factorise, and remember that a downward parabola is positive between its roots.

writtenQuestions.q:
For a sample of 17 inland towns in Australia, the height above sea level, x (metres), and the average maximum daily temperature, y (°C), were recorded.

The graph shows the data as well as a regression line.



The equation of the regression line is y = 29.2 − 0.011x.

The correlation coefficient is r = −0.494.

(a) (i) By using the equation of the regression line, predict the average maximum daily temperature, in degrees Celsius, for a town that is 540 m above sea level. Give your answer correct to one decimal place. (1 mark)

(a) (ii) The gradient of the regression line is −0.011. Interpret the value of this gradient in the given context. (2 marks)

(b) The graph below shows the relationship between the latitude, x (degrees south), and the average maximum daily temperature, y (°C), for the same 17 towns, as well as a regression line. (1 mark)



The equation of the regression line is y = 45.6 − 0.683x.

The correlation coefficient is r = −0.897.

Another inland town in Australia is 540 m above sea level. Its latitude is 28 degrees south.

Which measurement, height above sea level or latitude, would be better to use to predict this town’s average maximum daily temperature? Give a reason for your answer.
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a)(i) Substitute x = 540 into y = 29.2 − 0.011x:
y = 29.2 − 0.011(540) = 29.2 − 5.94 = 23.26
y = 23.3 °C (1 d.p.)

(a)(ii) For each extra metre above sea level, the average maximum daily temperature is predicted to fall by 0.011 °C. (Equivalently, a rise of 100 m in height corresponds to a fall of about 1.1 °C.)

(b) Latitude is the better predictor. Its correlation coefficient, r = −0.897, is much closer to −1 than the height's r = −0.494, so the relationship between latitude and temperature is far more strongly linear and the prediction from the latitude regression line is more reliable.

bandDescriptors.full: 23.3 °C; the gradient means temperature falls by 0.011 °C for each additional metre of height; latitude is better because |r| = 0.897 shows a much stronger linear relationship than |r| = 0.494.
bandDescriptors.partial: The prediction is correct and the gradient is interpreted as a decrease, but no units or context are given, or latitude is chosen without comparing the correlation coefficients.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Substitute the height into the equation. A gradient is a rate of change: how much y changes for a one-unit rise in x. To compare two models, compare how close each r is to −1 or 1.

writtenQuestions.q:
The diagram shows a triangle ABC where AC = 25 cm, BC = 16 cm, ∠BAC = 28° and angle ABC is obtuse.



Find the size of the obtuse angle ABC correct to the nearest degree.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Use the sine rule, pairing each side with the angle opposite it. AC is opposite ∠ABC and BC is opposite ∠BAC:

sin(∠ABC) / AC = sin(∠BAC) / BC
sin(∠ABC) / 25 = sin 28° / 16

sin(∠ABC) = 25 sin 28° ÷ 16 = 25 × 0.46947 ÷ 16 = 0.73355

The calculator gives ∠ABC = 47.19°, but the question states the angle is obtuse, and sin θ = sin(180° − θ), so take the second solution:
∠ABC = 180° − 47.19° = 132.81°

∠ABC = 133° (nearest degree)

bandDescriptors.full: ∠ABC = 133°, obtained from the sine rule and then taking the obtuse solution 180° − 47°.
bandDescriptors.partial: The sine rule is applied correctly to give sin(∠ABC) ≈ 0.7336, but the acute solution 47° is given instead of the obtuse one.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Use the sine rule with the side opposite each angle. When the angle is known to be obtuse, use the second solution, 180° minus the calculator value.

writtenQuestions.q: For what values of x, in the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ π/4, does the line y = 1 intersect the graph of y = 2 sin 4x?
writtenQuestions.answer:
Set the two expressions equal:
2 sin 4x = 1
sin 4x = 1/2

Let u = 4x. As x runs over 0 ≤ x ≤ π/4, u runs over 0 ≤ u ≤ π.

sin u = 1/2 has solutions u = π/6 and u = π − π/6 = 5π/6 in that range.

So 4x = π/6 or 4x = 5π/6, giving
x = π/24 or x = 5π/24

bandDescriptors.full: x = π/24 and x = 5π/24.
bandDescriptors.partial: sin 4x = 1/2 is obtained and one of the two solutions is found, usually π/24, with the second-quadrant solution missed.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Equate the two expressions and solve for sin 4x. Substituting u = 4x stretches the interval to 0 ≤ u ≤ π, which contains two angles with sine 1/2.

writtenQuestions.q:
A random variable is normally distributed with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. The table gives the probability that this random variable lies between 0 and z for different values of z.
z0.10.20.30.40.50.6
Probability0.03980.07930.11790.15540.19150.2257
The probability values given in the table for different values of z are represented by the shaded area in the following diagram.



(a) Using the table, find the probability that a value from a random variable that is normally distributed with mean 0 and standard deviation 1 lies between 0.1 and 0.5. (1 mark)

(b) Birth weights are normally distributed with a mean of 3300 grams and a standard deviation of 570 grams. By first calculating a z-score, find how many babies, out of 1000 born, are expected to have a birth weight greater than 3528 grams. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The table gives the area from 0 up to z. The strip between 0.1 and 0.5 is the difference of the two areas:

P(0.1 < Z < 0.5) = 0.1915 − 0.0398 = 0.1517

(b) Convert 3528 grams to a z-score:
z = (x − μ)/σ = (3528 − 3300)/570 = 228/570 = 0.4

The table gives P(0 < Z < 0.4) = 0.1554. Half of the distribution lies above the mean, so
P(Z > 0.4) = 0.5 − 0.1554 = 0.3446

Out of 1000 babies: 0.3446 × 1000 = 344.6

About 345 babies are expected to have a birth weight greater than 3528 grams.

bandDescriptors.partial: The z-score of 0.4 is correct and the table is read correctly, but 0.1554 is used directly instead of subtracting it from 0.5, or the result is not scaled to 1000.

A population, P, which is initially 5000, varies according to the formula

P = 5000b−t/10,

where b is a positive constant and t is time in years, t ≥ 0.

Step 1 — find b. At t = 20 the population is 1250:
1250 = 5000 b^(−2)
b^(−2) = 1/4, so b² = 4 and b = 2 (b is positive).

So P = 5000 × 2^(−t/10).

Step 2 — differentiate. For P = 5000 × 2^(kt), dP/dt = 5000 k (ln 2) 2^(kt) with k = −1/10:
dP/dt = −500 (ln 2) × 2^(−t/10)

Step 3 — set the rate of decrease to 30, so dP/dt = −30:
500 (ln 2) × 2^(−t/10) = 30
2^(−t/10) = 30 ÷ (500 ln 2) = 30 ÷ 346.5736 = 0.086563

Step 4 — solve for t by taking logarithms:
−t/10 = ln(0.086563) ÷ ln 2 = (−2.44679) ÷ 0.69315 = −3.52987
t = 35.2987…

t = 35.3 years (1 d.p.)

−5t² + 70t + 100 = 0

Velocity at that instant:
y′(7 + √69) = −10(7 + √69) + 70 = −70 − 10√69 + 70 = −10√69

Velocity = −10√69 m/s (that is, 10√69 ≈ 83.07 m/s downwards).

(b) E = ∫ₐᵇ 400 sin(πt/12) dt

The primitive of sin(kt) is −(1/k)cos(kt), with k = π/12, so 1/k = 12/π:

E = 400 × [−(12/π) cos(πt/12)]ₐᵇ
  = −(4800/π)[cos(bπ/12) − cos(aπ/12)]
  = (4800/π)(cos(aπ/12) − cos(bπ/12))   ✓

(c) Charging starts at a = 3 and must deliver 300 units:

300 = (4800/π)(cos(3π/12) − cos(bπ/12))
300π/4800 = cos(π/4) − cos(bπ/12)
0.196350 = 0.707107 − cos(bπ/12)
cos(bπ/12) = 0.510757
bπ/12 = 1.034812 radians
b = 1.034812 × 12/π = 3.95272 hours

Waiting time = 3.95272 − 3 = 0.95272 hours = 57.16 minutes

Charging from t = 3 begins at P(3) = 400 sin(π/4) ≈ 283 units per hour, well below the peak. Since the power is greater throughout the early part of the charge starting at t = 6, the same 300 units of energy accumulate in a shorter time.

(Check: from a = 6, cos(6π/12) = cos(π/2) = 0, so cos(bπ/12) = −0.196350, b = 6.7546 and the wait is 0.7546 h ≈ 45 minutes — less than 57.)

writtenQuestions.q: By considering the equation of the tangent to y = x² − 1 at the point (a, a² − 1), find the equations of the two tangents to y = x² − 1 which pass through (3, −8).

Step 1 — the general tangent. y′ = 2x, so the gradient at x = a is 2a.

y = 2ax − 2a² + a² − 1
y = 2ax − a² − 1

Step 2 — force it through (3, −8):
−8 = 2a(3) − a² − 1
−8 = 6a − a² − 1
a² − 6a − 7 = 0
(a − 7)(a + 1) = 0
a = 7 or a = −1

Step 3 — write the two tangents.
For a = 7: y = 14x − 49 − 1, that is y = 14x − 50
For a = −1: y = −2x − 1 − 1, that is y = −2x − 2

The two tangents are y = 14x − 50 and y = −2x − 2.

Check: at x = 3, 14(3) − 50 = −8 ✓ and −2(3) − 2 = −8 ✓

(a) A probability density function has total area 1:
∫₀⁶ Ax/(x² + 4) dx = 1

The numerator is half the derivative of the denominator, so the primitive is (A/2)ln(x² + 4):
(A/2)[ln(x² + 4)]₀⁶ = 1
(A/2)(ln 40 − ln 4) = 1
(A/2) ln 10 = 1
A = 2/ln 10   ✓

(b) The mode is the value of x at which f is greatest. Differentiate using the quotient rule:
f′(x) = A[(x² + 4)(1) − x(2x)]/(x² + 4)²
     = A(4 − x²)/(x² + 4)²

The denominator is always positive, so f′(x) = 0 when 4 − x² = 0, that is x = 2 (x = −2 is outside 0 ≤ x ≤ 6).

 = (A/2)[ln(x² + 4)]₀²
 = (A/2)(ln 8 − ln 4)
 = (A/2) ln 2
 = (1/ln 10) ln 2

P(H) = P(Z > 2) = 0.025

P(H | C) = P(C | H) × P(H) ÷ P(C)
        = 0.8 × 0.025 ÷ 0.301030
        = 0.02 ÷ 0.301030
        = 0.066438…

P(H | C) = 0.066 (3 d.p.)

a = 1/3.

k = 4 and a = 1/3, giving y = 4 sin(x/3).

bandDescriptors.full: k = 4 and a = 1/3, with the amplitude read from the maximum and a found from the period 6π.
bandDescriptors.partial: The amplitude is correct but a is wrong — a common slip is reading the period as 3π (the gap between consecutive zeros) rather than 6π (the gap between consecutive rising zeros).
bandDescriptors.minimal: Amplitude is the maximum height. The period of sin(ax) is 2π/a, and one full period runs from one upward crossing of the axis to the next.

writtenQuestions.q:
In a bag there are 3 six-sided dice. Two of the dice have faces marked 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The other is a special die with faces marked 1, 2, 3, 5, 5, 5.

One die is randomly selected and tossed.

(a) What is the probability that the die shows a 5? (1 mark)

(b) Given that the die shows a 5, what is the probability that it is the special die? (1 mark)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) P(ordinary die) = 2/3 and that die shows a 5 with probability 1/6.
P(special die) = 1/3 and that die shows a 5 with probability 3/6 = 1/2.

P(5) = (2/3)(1/6) + (1/3)(1/2)
= 2/18 + 3/18
= 5/18.

(b) P(special | 5) = P(special and 5) ÷ P(5)
= (3/18) ÷ (5/18)
= 3/5.

bandDescriptors.full: P(5) = 5/18 and P(special | 5) = 3/5.
bandDescriptors.partial: One part correct. A common slip in (a) is forgetting that two of the three dice are ordinary, so the ordinary branch carries weight 2/3, not 1/2.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Weight each die by the chance of selecting it: 2/3 for an ordinary die, 1/3 for the special one. Then (b) is P(special and 5) divided by the P(5) from (a).

writtenQuestions.q: The parabola y = x² meets the line y = 2x + 3 at the points (−1, 1) and (3, 9) as shown in the diagram.Find the area enclosed by the parabola and the line.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Between x = −1 and x = 3 the line lies above the parabola, so

Area = ∫₋₁³ [(2x + 3) − x²] dx
= [x² + 3x − x³/3]₋₁³

At x = 3: 9 + 9 − 9 = 9.
At x = −1: 1 − 3 + 1/3 = −5/3.

Area = 9 − (−5/3) = 32/3 square units (≈ 10.67 square units).

bandDescriptors.full: 32/3 square units, from ∫₋₁³ (2x + 3 − x²) dx.
bandDescriptors.partial: The integrand or the limits are right but an arithmetic slip follows — most often mishandling the negative lower limit, where x³/3 becomes +1/3.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The area between two curves is ∫ (upper − lower) dx between the points of intersection. Here the line is the upper curve on −1 ≤ x ≤ 3.

writtenQuestions.q:
Cards are stacked to build a ‘house of cards’. A house of cards with 3 rows is shown.

A house of cards requires 3 cards in the top row, 6 cards in the next row, and each successive row has 3 more cards than the previous row.(a) Show that a house of cards with 12 rows has a total of 234 cards. (2 marks)

(b) Another house of cards has a total of 828 cards.

How many rows are in this house of cards? (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
The rows form an arithmetic series with first term a = 3 and common difference d = 3.

(a) Sn = (n/2)[2a + (n − 1)d] = (n/2)[6 + 3(n − 1)] = 3n(n + 1)/2.

For n = 12: S₁₂ = 3 × 12 × 13 ÷ 2 = 468/2 = 234 cards, as required.

(b) Set 3n(n + 1)/2 = 828:
n(n + 1) = 552
n² + n − 552 = 0

n = (−1 + √(1 + 2208))/2 = (−1 + √2209)/2 = (−1 + 47)/2 = 23.
(The negative root is rejected.)

The house of cards has 23 rows.

bandDescriptors.full: (a) The arithmetic sum 3n(n + 1)/2 is derived and evaluated at n = 12 to give 234. (b) Solving 3n(n + 1)/2 = 828 gives n = 23 rows.
bandDescriptors.partial: Part (a) shown but the quadratic in (b) is not solved, or both roots are kept when only the positive one makes sense.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The row sizes 3, 6, 9, … form an arithmetic series with a = 3 and d = 3. Use Sn = (n/2)[2a + (n − 1)d], then set that sum equal to 828 and solve for n.

writtenQuestions.q:
(a) Differentiate y = (x² + 1)⁴. (2 marks)

(b) Hence, or otherwise, find ∫ x(x² + 1)³ dx. (1 mark)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Chain rule with u = x² + 1, so du/dx = 2x:
dy/dx = 4(x² + 1)³ × 2x
= 8x(x² + 1)³.

(b) Part (a) says the derivative of (x² + 1)⁴ is 8x(x² + 1)³, so
∫ 8x(x² + 1)³ dx = (x² + 1)⁴ + C.

Dividing by 8:
∫ x(x² + 1)³ dx = (1/8)(x² + 1)⁴ + C.

bandDescriptors.full: dy/dx = 8x(x² + 1)³ and ∫ x(x² + 1)³ dx = (1/8)(x² + 1)⁴ + C.
bandDescriptors.partial: The derivative is correct but the factor of 1/8 is dropped in (b), or the chain-rule factor 2x is omitted in (a).
bandDescriptors.minimal: Differentiate with the chain rule, then read (b) backwards from (a): the integrand is your derivative divided by 8, so the integral is (x² + 1)⁴ divided by 8.

writtenQuestions.q:
The graph of the function f(x) = x² is translated m units to the right, dilated vertically by a scale factor of k and then translated 5 units down. The equation of the transformed function is g(x) = 3x² − 12x + 7.

Find the values of m and k.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Apply the transformations in order:
translate m right:  (x − m)²
dilate vertically by k:  k(x − m)²
translate 5 down:  k(x − m)² − 5.

So g(x) = k(x − m)² − 5 = kx² − 2kmx + km² − 5.

Compare with 3x² − 12x + 7:
x² term: k = 3
x term: −2km = −12, so −6m = −12 and m = 2.

Check the constant: km² − 5 = 3(4) − 5 = 7 ✓

m = 2 and k = 3.

bandDescriptors.full: m = 2 and k = 3, obtained by writing g(x) = k(x − m)² − 5 and comparing coefficients (or by completing the square).
bandDescriptors.partial: k = 3 found from the x² coefficient but m not found, or the transformations applied in the wrong order so the −5 is dilated too.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Build the image step by step: x² → (x − m)² → k(x − m)² → k(x − m)² − 5. Then expand and match coefficients with 3x² − 12x + 7.

writtenQuestions.q:
A scientist is studying the growth of bacteria. The scientist models the number of bacteria, N, by the equation

N(t) = 200e0.013t,

where t is the number of hours after starting the experiment.

(a) What is the initial number of bacteria in the experiment? (1 mark)

(b) What is the number of bacteria 24 hours after starting the experiment? (1 mark)

(c) What is the rate of increase in the number of bacteria 24 hours after starting the experiment? (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Initially t = 0, so N(0) = 200e⁰ = 200 bacteria.

(b) N(24) = 200e^(0.013 × 24) = 200e^0.312 ≈ 200 × 1.36615 ≈ 273.23,
so about 273 bacteria.

(c) The rate of increase is N′(t):
N′(t) = 200 × 0.013 × e^(0.013t) = 2.6e^(0.013t).

N′(24) = 2.6e^0.312 ≈ 2.6 × 1.36615 ≈ 3.55,
so the number of bacteria is increasing at about 3.55 bacteria per hour.

bandDescriptors.full: 200 initially, about 273 after 24 hours, and a rate of about 3.55 bacteria per hour at t = 24.
bandDescriptors.partial: Parts (a) and (b) correct but (c) evaluates N(24) again instead of N′(24), or the chain-rule factor 0.013 is dropped when differentiating.
bandDescriptors.minimal: “Initial” means t = 0. A “rate of increase” is a derivative: differentiate N(t) = 200e^(0.013t) first, then substitute t = 24.

writtenQuestions.q:
Eli is choosing between two investment options.

Option 1: Depositing a single amount of $40 000 today, earning interest of 1.2% per annum, compounded monthly.

Option 2: Depositing $1000 at the end of each quarter, earning interest of 2.4% per annum, compounded quarterly.

A table of future value interest factors for an annuity of $1 is shown. N is the number of periods and the column headings give the interest rate r per period, as a decimal.
N0.0020.0060.0200.0240.0600.240
1010.0904810.2743710.9497211.1521113.1807931.64344
2020.3846021.1821124.2973725.2890936.78559303.60062
3030.8864632.7622740.5680843.2098379.058192640.91639
4041.6002645.0563060.4019865.92708154.7619722 728.80260
(a) What is the value of Eli’s investment after 10 years using Option 1? (2 marks)

(b) What is the difference between the future values after 10 years using Option 1 and Option 2? (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Option 1 is a single deposit with compound interest.
Rate per period r = 0.012 ÷ 12 = 0.001, and N = 10 × 12 = 120 periods.

FV = 40 000(1.001)¹²⁰
≈ 40 000 × 1.1274293
≈ $45 097.17.

(b) Option 2 is an annuity.
Rate per period r = 0.024 ÷ 4 = 0.006, and N = 10 × 4 = 40 periods.
From the table, the future value interest factor is 45.05630.

FV = 1000 × 45.05630 = $45 056.30.

Difference = 45 097.17 − 45 056.30 = $40.87.

bandDescriptors.full: Option 1 is about $45 097.17, Option 2 is $45 056.30 from the table factor 45.05630, and the difference is about $40.87.
bandDescriptors.partial: One of the two future values is correct. The most common slip is using the annual rate instead of the rate per period, or reading the table at r = 0.024 rather than r = 0.006.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Convert each annual rate to a rate per compounding period and count the periods in 10 years. Option 1 is a single deposit (compound interest); Option 2 is a series of equal deposits, so it uses the table factor.

writtenQuestions.q: Find the global maximum and minimum values of y = x³ − 6x² + 8, where −1 ≤ x ≤ 7.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Differentiate: dy/dx = 3x² − 12x = 3x(x − 4).

Stationary points where dy/dx = 0: x = 0 and x = 4. Both lie in −1 ≤ x ≤ 7.

Evaluate y at the stationary points and at both endpoints:
y(−1) = −1 − 6 + 8 = 1
y(0)  = 8
y(4)  = 64 − 96 + 8 = −24
y(7)  = 343 − 294 + 8 = 57

Global maximum: y = 57 at x = 7.
Global minimum:  y = −24 at x = 4.

bandDescriptors.full: Global maximum 57 at x = 7 and global minimum −24 at x = 4, with the endpoints tested as well as the stationary points.
bandDescriptors.partial: The stationary points are found but the endpoints are not tested, so the local maximum y = 8 at x = 0 is offered as the global maximum instead of 57.
bandDescriptors.minimal: On a closed interval the global extremes occur either at a stationary point or at an endpoint. Find both stationary points, then compare y at x = −1, 0, 4 and 7.

writtenQuestions.q:
The depth of water in a bay rises and falls with the tide. On a particular day the depth of the water, d metres, can be modelled by the equation

d = 1.3 − 0.6 cos(4πt/25),

where t is the time in hours since low tide.

(a) Find the depth of water at low tide and at high tide. (2 marks)

(b) What is the time interval, in hours, between two successive low tides? (1 mark)

(c) For how long between successive low tides will the depth of water be at least 1 metre? (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) cos takes values from −1 to 1.
Low tide: cos(4πt/25) = 1, so d = 1.3 − 0.6 = 0.7 m.
High tide: cos(4πt/25) = −1, so d = 1.3 + 0.6 = 1.9 m.

(b) The period is 2π ÷ (4π/25) = 2π × 25/(4π) = 12.5 hours.

(c) Require d ≥ 1:
1.3 − 0.6 cos(4πt/25) ≥ 1
−0.6 cos(4πt/25) ≥ −0.3
cos(4πt/25) ≤ 0.5.

Let θ = 4πt/25. Over one period 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π, cos θ ≤ 0.5 for π/3 ≤ θ ≤ 5π/3,
an interval of length 5π/3 − π/3 = 4π/3.

Since t = 25θ/(4π), the corresponding time is
(25/(4π)) × 4π/3 = 25/3 hours ≈ 8.33 hours (8 hours 20 minutes).

bandDescriptors.full: 0.7 m at low tide and 1.9 m at high tide, a 12.5 hour interval, and the depth is at least 1 m for 25/3 ≈ 8.33 hours.
bandDescriptors.partial: Parts (a) and (b) correct but (c) solves only for the first crossing rather than the whole interval, or the inequality sign is not reversed when dividing by −0.6.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The extremes come from cos = ±1. The period of cos(kt) is 2π/k. In (c), rearrange to cos(4πt/25) ≤ 0.5 — reversing the inequality when you divide by a negative — and find the whole range of angles that satisfy it.

writtenQuestions.q:
Jo is researching the relationship between the ages of teenage characters in television series and the ages of actors playing these characters.

After collecting the data, Jo finds that the correlation coefficient is 0.4564.

A scatterplot showing the data is drawn. The line of best fit with equation y = −7.51 + 1.85x, is also drawn.Describe and interpret the data and other information provided, with reference to the context given.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Form and direction: the scatterplot shows a positive, roughly linear association — older characters tend to be played by older actors.

Strength: r = 0.4564 is positive but only moderate, so the association is weak to moderate. The scatterplot supports this: at each character age the actors' ages are widely spread (for example, at 15 years the actors range from about 14 to 26), so the points do not cluster tightly about the line.

Gradient: 1.85 means that, on average, each extra year of character age is associated with about 1.85 extra years of actor age.

Intercept: −7.51 is the predicted actor age for a character aged 0. This has no meaning in context — it lies far outside the range of the data (character ages 14 to 17), so it is extrapolation.

Other features: nearly all the points lie above the line y = x, so actors are generally older than the characters they play — at a character age of 15 the line predicts about 20.3 years. The data cover only a narrow range of character ages, so predictions outside 14–17 years are unreliable, and the correlation shown does not establish that character age causes actor age.

bandDescriptors.full: Describes the positive, moderate, roughly linear association; interprets r = 0.4564, the gradient 1.85 and the intercept −7.51 in context; and notes that actors are generally older than their characters and that the narrow data range makes extrapolation unreliable.
bandDescriptors.partial: Describes the association and quotes the correlation coefficient, but does not interpret the gradient or the intercept in the context of ages, or treats the intercept −7.51 as if it were meaningful.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Comment on direction, form and strength of the association, then say what the gradient 1.85 and the intercept −7.51 mean for actors and characters — and whether the intercept makes sense given the character ages actually in the data.

writtenQuestions.q:
Let f(x) = sin(2x).

Find the value of x, for 0 < x < π, for which f′(x) = −√3 AND f″(x) = 2.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Differentiate twice:
f′(x) = 2 cos 2x
f″(x) = −4 sin 2x

First condition: 2 cos 2x = −√3, so cos 2x = −√3/2.
Second condition: −4 sin 2x = 2, so sin 2x = −1/2.

Both cos 2x and sin 2x are negative, so 2x lies in the third quadrant. The reference angle with cosine √3/2 and sine 1/2 is π/6, so
2x = π + π/6 = 7π/6.

Since 0 < x < π gives 0 < 2x < 2π, this is the only solution.

x = 7π/12.

bandDescriptors.full: x = 7π/12, from cos 2x = −√3/2 and sin 2x = −1/2 placing 2x = 7π/6.
bandDescriptors.partial: Both derivatives correct and one equation solved, but the two conditions are not combined — solving cos 2x = −√3/2 alone gives 2x = 5π/6 as well, which the sine condition rules out.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Differentiate twice, then use both conditions together. The signs of sin 2x and cos 2x fix which quadrant 2x is in; only then halve to get x.

writtenQuestions.q:
The life span of batteries from a particular factory is normally distributed with a mean of 840 hours and a standard deviation of 80 hours.

It is known from statistical tables that for this distribution approximately 60% of the batteries have a life span of less than 860 hours.

What is the approximate percentage of batteries with a life span between 820 and 920 hours?
writtenQuestions.answer:
Standardise each value with z = (x − μ)/σ, where μ = 840 and σ = 80.

860 → z = 20/80 = 0.25, and we are told P(Z < 0.25) ≈ 0.60.
820 → z = −20/80 = −0.25
920 → z = 80/80 = 1

By symmetry, P(Z < −0.25) = 1 − P(Z < 0.25) = 1 − 0.60 = 0.40.

From the empirical rule, 68% of values lie within one standard deviation, so
P(Z < 1) = 0.5 + 0.34 = 0.84.

P(820 < X < 920) = P(−0.25 < Z < 1)
= 0.84 − 0.40
= 0.44.

About 44% of the batteries.

bandDescriptors.partial: One of the two tail probabilities is found correctly. A common slip is taking P(Z < −0.25) as 0.60 rather than using symmetry to get 0.40.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Standardise all three values. The given 60% fixes P(Z < 0.25); symmetry then gives P(Z < −0.25). Use the empirical 68% rule for z = 1, then subtract.

writtenQuestions.q:
Let f(x) = xe−2x.

It is given that f′(x) = e−2x − 2xe−2x.

(a) Show that f″(x) = 4(x − 1)e−2x. (2 marks)

(b) Find any stationary points of f(x) and determine their nature. (2 marks)

Part (c), which asked for the curve y = xe−2x to be sketched showing stationary points, points of inflection and intercepts, is not included here.
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Differentiate f′(x) = e⁻²ˣ − 2xe⁻²ˣ term by term.

d/dx (e⁻²ˣ) = −2e⁻²ˣ
d/dx (2xe⁻²ˣ) = 2e⁻²ˣ + 2x(−2e⁻²ˣ) = 2e⁻²ˣ − 4xe⁻²ˣ  (product rule)

So f″(x) = −2e⁻²ˣ − (2e⁻²ˣ − 4xe⁻²ˣ)
= −4e⁻²ˣ + 4xe⁻²ˣ
= 4(x − 1)e⁻²ˣ, as required.

(b) Stationary points where f′(x) = 0:
e⁻²ˣ(1 − 2x) = 0.
e⁻²ˣ is never zero, so 1 − 2x = 0 and x = 1/2.

y-value: f(1/2) = (1/2)e⁻¹ = 1/(2e) ≈ 0.184.

Nature: f″(1/2) = 4(1/2 − 1)e⁻¹ = −2e⁻¹ < 0, so the curve is concave down there.

There is a single stationary point, a maximum at (1/2, 1/(2e)).

bandDescriptors.full: f″(x) = 4(x − 1)e⁻²ˣ shown, and a maximum turning point at (1/2, 1/(2e)) confirmed by f″(1/2) < 0.
bandDescriptors.partial: The second derivative is shown but the stationary point's nature is not determined, or x = 1/2 is found without its y-coordinate.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Differentiate f′ using the product rule on the 2xe⁻²ˣ term. For (b), factor e⁻²ˣ out of f′ — it is never zero, so only 1 − 2x = 0 matters — then test the sign of f″ there.

omittedParts.reason: The student must sketch the curve y = xe⁻²ˣ, showing stationary points, points of inflection and intercepts with the axes. The engine cannot accept or mark a hand-drawn graph.

writtenQuestions.q:
The graph of the circle x² + y² = 2 is shown.

The interval connecting the origin, O, and the point (1, 1) makes an angle θ with the positive x-axis.(a) By considering the value of θ, find the exact area of the shaded region, as shown on the diagram. (2 marks)

Part of the hyperbola y = a/(b − x) − 1 which passes through the points (0, 0) and (1, 1) is drawn with the circle x² + y² = 2 as shown.(b) Show that a = b = 2. (2 marks)

(c) Using parts (a) and (b), find the exact area of the region bounded by the hyperbola, the positive x-axis and the circle as shown on the diagram. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The point (1, 1) gives tan θ = 1/1, so θ = π/4. The circle has radius √2, so r² = 2.

Sector Oxy from the positive x-axis round to (1, 1):
Area = ½r²θ = ½ × 2 × π/4 = π/4.

The shaded region is that sector with the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (1, 0) and (1, 1) removed:
Triangle area = ½ × 1 × 1 = ½.

Shaded area = π/4 − ½ square units.

(b) Through (0, 0):  0 = a/(b − 0) − 1, so a/b = 1 and a = b.
Through (1, 1):  1 = a/(b − 1) − 1, so a/(b − 1) = 2 and a = 2b − 2.

Substituting a = b:  b = 2b − 2, so b = 2 and hence a = 2, as required.

(c) With a = b = 2 the hyperbola is y = 2/(2 − x) − 1.

Area under the hyperbola from x = 0 to x = 1:
∫₀¹ [2/(2 − x) − 1] dx = [−2 ln(2 − x) − x]₀¹
= (−2 ln 1 − 1) − (−2 ln 2 − 0)
= 2 ln 2 − 1.

From x = 1 to x = √2 the region is bounded above by the circle, and that piece is exactly the shaded region from part (a): π/4 − ½.

Total area = (2 ln 2 − 1) + (π/4 − ½)
= 2 ln 2 + π/4 − 3/2 square units.

bandDescriptors.full: (a) π/4 − ½. (b) a = b = 2 shown from both given points. (c) 2 ln 2 + π/4 − 3/2 square units, built from the integral of the hyperbola plus the region from part (a).
bandDescriptors.partial: Parts (a) and (b) correct but (c) integrates the hyperbola only, missing the circular piece from x = 1 to x = √2, or forgets to subtract the triangle in (a).
bandDescriptors.minimal: In (a), θ = π/4 and r² = 2, so use ½r²θ for the sector and subtract the right-angled triangle. In (b), substitute both points to get two equations in a and b. In (c), split the region at x = 1 and reuse (a) for the right-hand piece.

writtenQuestions.q:
(a) The diagram shows the graph of y = 2−x. Also shown on the diagram are the first 5 of an infinite number of rectangular strips of width 1 unit and height y = 2−x for non-negative integer values of x. For example, the second rectangle shown has width 1 and height ½.The sum of the areas of the rectangles forms a geometric series.

Show that the limiting sum of this series is 2. (1 mark)

(b) Show that ∫₀⁴ 2−x dx = 15/(16 ln 2). (2 marks)

(c) Use parts (a) and (b) to show that e15 < 232. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The rectangles have width 1 and heights 2⁰, 2⁻¹, 2⁻², … so their areas are 1, ½, ¼, …

This is a geometric series with a = 1 and r = ½, and |r| < 1, so
S∞ = a/(1 − r) = 1/(1 − ½) = 2, as required.

(b) ∫ 2⁻ˣ dx = −2⁻ˣ/ln 2, so
∫₀⁴ 2⁻ˣ dx = [−2⁻ˣ/ln 2]₀⁴
= (−2⁻⁴ + 2⁰)/ln 2
= (1 − 1/16)/ln 2
= 15/(16 ln 2), as required.

(c) The first four rectangles cover 0 ≤ x ≤ 4. Their total area is the limiting sum from (a) less the rectangles from x = 4 onwards:
1 + ½ + ¼ + ⅛ = 2 − (1/16 + 1/32 + …) = 2 − ⅛ = 15/8.

Because 2⁻ˣ is decreasing, each rectangle sits above the curve, so the rectangles overestimate the area:
15/8 > ∫₀⁴ 2⁻ˣ dx = 15/(16 ln 2).

Divide both sides by 15 and rearrange:
1/8 > 1/(16 ln 2)
16 ln 2 > 8
ln 2 > ½.

Multiply by 32:  32 ln 2 > 16 > 15,
so ln(2³²) > 15 and therefore 2³² > e¹⁵, that is e¹⁵ < 2³².

bandDescriptors.full: (a) a = 1, r = ½ and S∞ = 2. (b) The antiderivative −2⁻ˣ/ln 2 evaluated from 0 to 4 gives 15/(16 ln 2). (c) The rectangles overestimate the integral, giving 15/8 > 15/(16 ln 2), hence ln 2 > ½ and e¹⁵ < 2³².
bandDescriptors.partial: Parts (a) and (b) shown but (c) does not compare the correct four-rectangle sum 15/8 with the integral, or the inequality is reversed when dividing.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The rectangle areas form a geometric series with r = ½. For (b), the antiderivative of aˣ is aˣ/ln a. For (c), note the rectangles lie above the decreasing curve, so their total area exceeds the integral over the same interval.

writtenQuestions.q:
A continuous random variable X has cumulative distribution function given by
{1,   x > e³
(1/k) ln x,   1 ≤ x ≤ e³
0,   x < 1


(a) Show that k = 3. (1 mark)

(b) Given that P(X < c) = 2P(X > c), find the exact value of c. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) A cumulative distribution function must reach 1 at the top of its range, and F must be continuous there.

At x = e³:  F(e³) = (1/k) ln(e³) = 3/k.
Setting 3/k = 1 gives k = 3, as required.

(b) With k = 3, F(x) = (1/3) ln x for 1 ≤ x ≤ e³.

P(X < c) = F(c) and P(X > c) = 1 − F(c), so
F(c) = 2[1 − F(c)]
3F(c) = 2
F(c) = 2/3.

Hence (1/3) ln c = 2/3, so ln c = 2 and
c = e².

(This lies in the range, since 1 ≤ e² ≤ e³.)

bandDescriptors.full: k = 3 from F(e³) = 1, and c = e² from F(c) = 2/3.
bandDescriptors.partial: k = 3 shown but (b) sets F(c) = 2/3 incorrectly — for instance solving F(c) = 2 or splitting the probability as ⅓ and ⅔ the wrong way round.
bandDescriptors.minimal: A cumulative distribution function reaches 1 at the top of its range. In (b), P(X > c) = 1 − F(c), so the condition becomes F(c) = 2[1 − F(c)].

writtenQuestions.q:
A line passes through the point P(1, 2) and meets the axes at X(x, 0) and Y(0, y), where x > 1.(a) Show that y = 2x/(x − 1). (2 marks)

(b) Find the minimum value of the area of triangle XOY. (4 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) X, P and Y are collinear, so the gradient from Y to P equals the gradient from P to X.

Gradient YP = (2 − y)/(1 − 0) = 2 − y
Gradient PX = (0 − 2)/(x − 1) = −2/(x − 1)

Set them equal:
2 − y = −2/(x − 1)
y = 2 + 2/(x − 1)
= [2(x − 1) + 2]/(x − 1)
= 2x/(x − 1), as required.

(b) Triangle XOY is right-angled at the origin with legs x and y, so
A = ½xy = ½ × x × 2x/(x − 1) = x²/(x − 1).

Differentiate with the quotient rule:
dA/dx = [2x(x − 1) − x²]/(x − 1)²
= (x² − 2x)/(x − 1)²
= x(x − 2)/(x − 1)².

dA/dx = 0 for x > 1 gives x = 2.

For 1 < x < 2, dA/dx < 0; for x > 2, dA/dx > 0. So x = 2 gives a minimum.

Minimum area = 2²/(2 − 1) = 4 square units.

bandDescriptors.full: (a) y = 2x/(x − 1) from equal gradients through P. (b) A = x²/(x − 1), dA/dx = x(x − 2)/(x − 1)², minimum at x = 2 giving area 4 square units.
bandDescriptors.partial: The area function is set up and differentiated but x = 0 is kept as a solution (it is outside x > 1), or the minimum is not verified.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Use the fact that X, P and Y lie on one line to link x and y. Then the triangle's area is ½xy — write it in terms of x alone and minimise it for x > 1.

writtenQuestions.q:
In a reducing-balance loan, an amount $P is borrowed for a period of n months at an interest rate of 0.25% per month, compounded monthly. At the end of each month, a repayment of $M is made. After the nth repayment has been made, the amount owing, $An, is given by

An = P(1.0025)n − M(1 + (1.0025)¹ + (1.0025)² + … + (1.0025)n−1).

(Do NOT prove this.)

(a) Jane borrows $200 000 in a reducing-balance loan as described.

The loan is to be repaid in 180 monthly repayments.

Show that M = 1381.16, when rounded to the nearest cent. (2 marks)

(b) After 100 repayments of $1381.16 have been made, the interest rate changes to 0.35% per month.

At this stage, the amount owing to the nearest dollar is $100 032. (Do NOT prove this.)

Jane continues to make the same monthly repayments.

For how many more months will Jane need to make full monthly payments of $1381.16? (3 marks)

(c) The final repayment will be less than $1381.16.

How much will Jane need to pay in the final payment in order to pay off the loan? (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The bracket is a geometric series with a = 1, r = 1.0025 and 180 terms, so it sums to (1.0025¹⁸⁰ − 1)/0.0025.

The loan is repaid when A₁₈₀ = 0:
200 000(1.0025)¹⁸⁰ = M(1.0025¹⁸⁰ − 1)/0.0025

1.0025¹⁸⁰ ≈ 1.5674336, so
M = 200 000 × 0.0025 × 1.5674336 ÷ 0.5674336
= 783.7168 ÷ 0.5674336
≈ 1381.1633

M = $1381.16 when rounded to the nearest cent.

(b) Restart with P = 100 032, r = 0.0035 and M = 1381.16. Let x = 1.0035ⁿ.

A_n = 100 032x − 1381.16(x − 1)/0.0035 = 0
100 032x = 394 617.14(x − 1)
394 617.14 = 294 585.14x
x = 1.339569

n = ln(1.339569) ÷ ln(1.0035) ≈ 0.292348 ÷ 0.0034939 ≈ 83.67.

So after 83 more full repayments there is still a small amount owing, and the 84th payment is smaller than a full one.

Jane needs to make 83 more full monthly payments of $1381.16.

(c) Amount owing after those 83 repayments:
A₈₃ = 100 032(1.0035)⁸³ − 1381.16 × [(1.0035)⁸³ − 1]/0.0035
≈ 133 679.6 − 132 751.3
≈ $928.29

One more month's interest is charged before the final payment:
Final payment = 928.29 × 1.0035 ≈ $931.54.

bandDescriptors.full: (a) M = $1381.16 from A₁₈₀ = 0. (b) n ≈ 83.67, so 83 more full repayments. (c) A₈₃ ≈ $928.29 and the final payment is about $931.54.
bandDescriptors.partial: Parts (a) and (b) correct but the answer to (b) is rounded up to 84, or (c) gives the balance $928.29 without adding the final month's interest.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Sum the bracket as a geometric series, then set A_n = 0 to find M. In (b), restart the same formula with the new rate, the new balance and the same repayment, and solve for n — then read the non-integer answer carefully: a partial month is not a full payment.

writtenQuestions.q:
Let P(t) be a function such that dP/dt = 3000e2t.

When t = 0, P = 4000.

Find an expression for P(t).

bandDescriptors.full: P(t) = 1500e²ᵗ + 2500 — correct antiderivative and the constant found from P(0) = 4000.

writtenQuestions.q: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve y = (2x + 1)³ at the point (0, 1).
writtenQuestions.answer:
Differentiate with the chain rule:
dy/dx = 3(2x + 1)² × 2 = 6(2x + 1)².
At x = 0: dy/dx = 6(1)² = 6, so the tangent has gradient 6.
Using y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) at (0, 1):
y − 1 = 6(x − 0)
y = 6x + 1.

bandDescriptors.full: y = 6x + 1, with the gradient 6 found by correctly applying the chain rule at x = 0.
bandDescriptors.partial: The derivative is correct but the tangent equation is not formed properly, or the factor of 2 from the chain rule is dropped (giving gradient 3).
bandDescriptors.minimal: Differentiate (2x + 1)³ with the chain rule — the derivative of the inside, 2, is a factor. Then substitute x = 0 for the gradient and use the point (0, 1).

contribution = 450 000 ÷ 13.181 = 34 140.05…
Micky should contribute $34 140 each year.

(b) Compounding quarterly for 10 years gives 40 periods at a rate of 6% ÷ 4 = 1.5% per period.
The factor for 40 periods at 1.5% is 54.268.
Future value = 8535 × 54.268 = 463 177.38.
Micky will have $463 177.38 at the end of 10 years.

writtenQuestions.q:
The diagram shows a shape APQBCD. The shape consists of a rectangle ABCD with an arc PQ on side AB and with side lengths BC = 3.6 m and CD = 8.0 m.

The arc PQ is an arc of a circle with centre O and radius 2.1 m and ∠POQ = 110°.What is the perimeter of the shape APQBCD? Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
writtenQuestions.answer:
The perimeter is AP + arc PQ + QB + BC + CD + DA.

Chord PQ (using the cosine rule, or twice the half-chord):
PQ = 2 × 2.1 × sin 55° = 3.4404… m
AP + QB = AB − PQ = 8.0 − 3.4404 = 4.5596 m

Arc PQ = rθ with θ in radians:
θ = 110 × π/180 = 1.9199 radians
arc = 2.1 × 1.9199 = 4.0317 m

Perimeter = 4.5596 + 4.0317 + 3.6 + 8.0 + 3.6
= 23.791…
≈ 23.8 m.

bandDescriptors.full: 23.8 m, with the chord PQ subtracted from AB and the arc length rθ added in its place.
bandDescriptors.partial: Arc length and chord both found but combined incorrectly — commonly the whole of AB is counted as well as the arc, or the chord is added rather than subtracted.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Walk the boundary: A to P, along the arc to Q, Q to B, then the three rectangle sides. AP + QB is 8.0 minus the straight chord PQ, and the arc itself is rθ with θ in radians.

writtenQuestions.q: Find ∫ x√(x² + 1) dx.
writtenQuestions.answer:
The derivative of x² + 1 is 2x, and the integrand already contains an x, so reverse the chain rule.
∫ x(x² + 1)^(1/2) dx = ½ ∫ 2x(x² + 1)^(1/2) dx
= ½ × (2/3)(x² + 1)^(3/2) + C
= (1/3)(x² + 1)^(3/2) + C.

Check by differentiating: (1/3) × (3/2)(x² + 1)^(1/2) × 2x = x√(x² + 1).

bandDescriptors.partial: The power (3/2) is right but the coefficient is wrong — usually the ½ that compensates for the missing 2x is left out, or + C is omitted.
bandDescriptors.minimal: This is a reverse chain rule: the x outside is (half of) the derivative of x² + 1. Raise the power by one to 3/2 and divide by 3/2, then fix the constant.

writtenQuestions.q:
A university uses gas to heat its buildings. Over a period of 10 weekdays during winter, the gas used each day was measured in megawatts (MW) and the average outside temperature each day was recorded in degrees Celsius (°C).

Using x as the average daily outside temperature and y as the total daily gas usage, the equation of the least-squares regression line was found.

The equation of the regression line predicts that when the temperature is 0°C, the daily gas usage is 236 MW.

The ten temperatures measured were: 0°, 0°, 0°, 2°, 5°, 7°, 8°, 9°, 9°, 10°.

The total gas usage for the ten weekdays was 1840 MW.

In any bivariate dataset, the least-squares regression line passes through the point (x̄, ȳ), where x̄ is the sample mean of the x-values and ȳ is the sample mean of the y-values.

(b) What is the equation of the regression line? (2 marks)

(c) In the context of the dataset, identify ONE problem with using the regression line to predict gas usage when the average outside temperature is 23°C. (1 mark)

Part (a), which asked for the point (x̄, ȳ) and the y-intercept to be plotted on a printed grid, is not included here — work with the numbers directly.
writtenQuestions.answer:
(b) x̄ = (0 + 0 + 0 + 2 + 5 + 7 + 8 + 9 + 9 + 10) ÷ 10 = 50/10 = 5
ȳ = 1840/10 = 184
The line passes through (5, 184), and its y-intercept is (0, 236).
Gradient = (184 − 236)/(5 − 0) = −52/5 = −10.4
y = −10.4x + 236.

(c) The temperatures in the dataset run only from 0°C to 10°C, so predicting at 23°C is extrapolation — well outside the range of the data. There is no evidence the linear relationship continues that far, and the line in fact predicts a negative gas usage (236 − 10.4 × 23 ≈ −4 MW), which is impossible.

bandDescriptors.full: y = −10.4x + 236 in (b), from the means (5, 184) and the intercept (0, 236); and (c) identifies extrapolation beyond the 0–10°C range of the data.
bandDescriptors.partial: The means are found but the gradient is wrong (often the sign), or (c) says only that the answer 'looks wrong' without naming extrapolation.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The regression line passes through (x̄, ȳ), and the intercept gives a second point (0, 236). Two points give the gradient. For (c), compare 23°C with the largest temperature actually measured.

omittedParts.reason: The student must plot the point (x̄, ȳ) and the y-intercept of the least-squares regression line on a printed grid. The engine cannot accept or mark points plotted by hand.

writtenQuestions.q:
(b) Hence, or otherwise, solve the inequality x − 1 < (1 − x)(3 + x). (2 marks)

Part (a), which asked for the graphs of f(x) = x − 1 and g(x) = (1 − x)(3 + x) to be sketched on a printed grid showing the x-intercepts, is not included here — solve part (b) algebraically.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Expand the right-hand side:
(1 − x)(3 + x) = 3 + x − 3x − x² = 3 − 2x − x²

x − 1 < 3 − 2x − x²
x² + x + 2x − 1 − 3 < 0
x² + 3x − 4 < 0
(x + 4)(x − 1) < 0

The parabola is concave up with roots −4 and 1, so it is negative between them:
−4 < x < 1.

writtenQuestions.q: Find all the values of θ, where 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, such that sin(θ − 60°) = −√3/2.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Let u = θ − 60°. As θ runs from 0° to 360°, u runs from −60° to 300°.

sin u = −√3/2, so the related angle is 60° and u lies in the third or fourth quadrant.
In −60° ≤ u ≤ 300° the solutions are
u = −60°, u = 180° + 60° = 240°, and u = 360° − 60° = 300°.

Therefore θ = u + 60° gives
θ = 0°, 300°, 360°.

bandDescriptors.full: θ = 0°, 300° and 360° — all three, found by shifting the domain to −60° ≤ θ − 60° ≤ 300°.
bandDescriptors.partial: Two of the three values found — typically the endpoints 0° and 360° are missed because the shifted domain was not used.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Substitute u = θ − 60° and shift the domain with it, so u runs from −60° to 300°. The related angle is 60° and sine is negative in the third and fourth quadrants.

Then in triangle AEM,
tan ∠AEM = AM/AE = √58/8
∠AEM = tan⁻¹(0.95197…)
= 43.59°

writtenQuestions.q:
A gardener wants to build a rectangular garden of area 50 m² against an existing wall as shown in the diagram. A concrete path of width 1 metre is to be built around the other three sides of the garden.Let x and y be the dimensions, in metres, of the outer rectangle as shown.

(a) Show that y = 50/(x − 2) + 1. (1 mark)

(b) Find the value of x such that the area of the concrete path is a minimum. Show that your answer gives a minimum area. (4 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The path is 1 m wide on both ends and along the bottom, so the garden measures (x − 2) by (y − 1).
(x − 2)(y − 1) = 50
y − 1 = 50/(x − 2)
y = 50/(x − 2) + 1.

(b) Area of path A = xy − 50
= x[50/(x − 2) + 1] − 50
= 50x/(x − 2) + x − 50.

Differentiate, using the quotient rule on the first term:
d/dx [50x/(x − 2)] = [50(x − 2) − 50x]/(x − 2)² = −100/(x − 2)²
dA/dx = 1 − 100/(x − 2)².

Set dA/dx = 0:
(x − 2)² = 100, so x − 2 = 10 (taking the positive root, since x > 2)
x = 12.

Second derivative: d²A/dx² = 200/(x − 2)³, which at x = 12 is 200/1000 = 0.2 > 0, so the stationary point is a minimum.

x = 12 m.

bandDescriptors.full: y = 50/(x − 2) + 1 derived from the garden's dimensions, then x = 12 from dA/dx = 0 with a positive second derivative confirming a minimum.
bandDescriptors.partial: The area function is set up and differentiated correctly but the minimum is not justified, or the negative root x − 2 = −10 is kept.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The garden is (x − 2) by (y − 1) — the path takes 1 m from each end and 1 m from the bottom, but not from the wall side. The path's area is the outer rectangle minus 50.

writtenQuestions.q:
A camera films the motion of a swing in a park.

Let x(t) be the horizontal distance, in metres, from the camera to the seat of the swing at t seconds.

The seat is released from rest at a horizontal distance of 11.2 m from the camera.(a) The rate of change of x can be modelled by the equation dx/dt = −1.5π sin(5πt/4).

Find an expression for x(t). (2 marks)

(b) How many times does the swing reach the closest point to the camera during the first 10 seconds? (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) x(t) = ∫ −1.5π sin(5πt/4) dt
= −1.5π × [−cos(5πt/4)] ÷ (5π/4) + C
= (1.5π × 4)/(5π) × cos(5πt/4) + C
= 1.2 cos(5πt/4) + C.

Released from rest at 11.2 m means x(0) = 11.2:
1.2 cos 0 + C = 11.2, so 1.2 + C = 11.2 and C = 10.
x(t) = 1.2 cos(5πt/4) + 10.

(b) The closest point to the camera is the minimum of x, where cos(5πt/4) = −1, that is 5πt/4 = π, 3π, 5π, …
t = 0.8, 2.4, 4.0, 5.6, 7.2, 8.8, 10.4, … (one every full period of 2π ÷ (5π/4) = 1.6 seconds)

Within the first 10 seconds: t = 0.8, 2.4, 4.0, 5.6, 7.2, 8.8 — 6 times.

bandDescriptors.full: x(t) = 1.2 cos(5πt/4) + 10, then 6 times in the first 10 seconds.
bandDescriptors.partial: The integration is correct but the constant is not found from x(0) = 11.2, or the count in (b) is out by one — t = 10.4 lies outside the 10 seconds.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Antidifferentiate sin(kt) to −cos(kt)/k. Then the closest approach is the minimum of x, once per period, and the period is 2π ÷ (5π/4) = 1.6 seconds.

writtenQuestions.q:
The graph of y = f(x), where f(x) = a|x − b| + c, passes through the points (3, −5), (6, 7) and (9, −5) as shown in the diagram.(a) Find the values of a, b and c. (3 marks)

(b) The line y = mx cuts the graph of y = f(x) in two distinct places.

Find all possible values of m. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The graph is symmetric about its vertex, which the diagram shows at (6, 7). For y = a|x − b| + c the vertex is (b, c), so b = 6 and c = 7.
Substitute (3, −5):
a|3 − 6| + 7 = −5
3a = −12, so a = −4.
a = −4, b = 6, c = 7.

(b) f(x) = −4|x − 6| + 7 has two straight branches:
left branch (x < 6): y = 4x − 17
right branch (x ≥ 6): y = −4x + 31

The line y = mx passes through the origin. It meets the right branch where mx = −4x + 31, that is x = 31/(m + 4), and that intersection lies on the branch (x ≥ 6) only when −4 < m ≤ 7/6.
It meets the left branch where mx = 4x − 17, that is x = 17/(4 − m), and that lies on the branch (x < 6) only when m < 7/6 or m > 4.

Both branches are cut, in distinct points, exactly when
−4 < m < 7/6.

(At m = 7/6 the line passes through the vertex (6, 7) and touches at a single point; at m = −4 the line is parallel to the right branch.)

bandDescriptors.full: a = −4, b = 6, c = 7 in (a), and −4 < m < 7/6 in (b), with both endpoints correctly excluded.
bandDescriptors.partial: (a) fully correct but (b) gives only one boundary, or includes an endpoint — at m = 7/6 the line passes through the vertex and meets the graph once, and at m = −4 it is parallel to a branch.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The vertex of y = a|x − b| + c is (b, c), which the diagram gives directly. For (b), write the two branches as separate straight lines and ask when y = mx meets each one on its own side of x = 6.

writtenQuestions.q:
The curve y = f(x) is shown on the diagram. The equation of the tangent to the curve at point T(−1, 6) is y = x + 7. At a point R, another tangent parallel to the tangent at T is drawn.The gradient function of the curve is given by dy/dx = 3x² − 6x − 8.

Find the coordinates of R.
writtenQuestions.answer:
The tangent at T has gradient 1, so at R the gradient is also 1:
3x² − 6x − 8 = 1
3x² − 6x − 9 = 0
x² − 2x − 3 = 0
(x − 3)(x + 1) = 0, so x = 3 or x = −1.
x = −1 is the point T, so R has x = 3.

To find the y-value, antidifferentiate:
y = x³ − 3x² − 8x + C
T(−1, 6) lies on the curve: −1 − 3 + 8 + C = 6, so C = 2.
y = x³ − 3x² − 8x + 2

At x = 3: y = 27 − 27 − 24 + 2 = −22.

R = (3, −22).

bandDescriptors.full: R = (3, −22) — x = 3 from equating the gradient function to 1, and y from antidifferentiating and using T(−1, 6) to find the constant.
bandDescriptors.partial: x = 3 found but the y-value is wrong, usually because the constant of integration was omitted or found from the tangent rather than the curve.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Parallel tangents have equal gradients, and the tangent at T is y = x + 7, so its gradient is 1. Set the gradient function equal to 1 for the x-value, then antidifferentiate and use T to fix + C.

writtenQuestions.q:
A continuous random variable X has probability density function f(x) given by
{12x²(1 − x),   for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1
0,   for all other values of x


(a) Find the mode of X. (2 marks)

(b) Find the cumulative distribution function for the given probability density function. (2 marks)

(c) Without calculating the median, show that the mode is greater than the median. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The mode is where f is greatest. Expand: f(x) = 12x² − 12x³.
f′(x) = 24x − 36x² = 12x(2 − 3x)
f′(x) = 0 at x = 0 and x = 2/3. Since f′ changes from positive to negative at x = 2/3, that is the maximum.
Mode = 2/3.

(b) For 0 ≤ x ≤ 1,
F(x) = ∫₀ˣ (12t² − 12t³) dt = [4t³ − 3t⁴]₀ˣ = 4x³ − 3x⁴.
So F(x) = 0 for x < 0, F(x) = 4x³ − 3x⁴ for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, and F(x) = 1 for x > 1.
(Check: F(1) = 4 − 3 = 1.)

(c) Evaluate F at the mode:
F(2/3) = 4(8/27) − 3(16/81) = 32/27 − 16/27 = 16/27 ≈ 0.593.
That is more than 0.5, so more than half the probability lies below x = 2/3. F is increasing, so the median — the value where F = 0.5 — must lie to the left of 2/3.
Therefore the mode is greater than the median.

bandDescriptors.full: Mode 2/3, F(x) = 4x³ − 3x⁴ on [0, 1], and F(2/3) = 16/27 > 0.5 used to place the median below the mode.
bandDescriptors.partial: Mode and cumulative distribution function correct, but (c) attempts to solve for the median instead of comparing F(2/3) with 0.5.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The mode maximises f, so solve f′(x) = 0. The cumulative distribution function is ∫₀ˣ f(t) dt. For (c), the median is where F = 0.5 — so just work out F at the mode and compare.

writtenQuestions.q:
Let f(x) = e−x sin x.

(a) Find the coordinates of the stationary points of f(x) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π. You do NOT need to check the nature of the stationary points. (3 marks)

Part (b), which asked for the graph of y = f(x) to be sketched on a printed set of axes showing stationary points and intercepts, is not included here.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Differentiate with the product rule:
f′(x) = −e⁻ˣ sin x + e⁻ˣ cos x
= e⁻ˣ(cos x − sin x).

e⁻ˣ is never zero, so f′(x) = 0 when cos x = sin x, that is tan x = 1.
For 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π: x = π/4 and x = 5π/4.

f(π/4) = e^(−π/4) × √2/2 ≈ 0.322
f(5π/4) = e^(−5π/4) × (−√2/2) ≈ −0.014

Stationary points: (π/4, (√2/2)e^(−π/4)) ≈ (0.785, 0.322) and (5π/4, −(√2/2)e^(−5π/4)) ≈ (3.927, −0.014).

bandDescriptors.full: Both stationary points, x = π/4 and x = 5π/4, with their y-coordinates.
bandDescriptors.partial: The derivative and tan x = 1 are correct but only one solution is given in the domain, or the y-coordinates are not found.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Use the product rule, then factor out e⁻ˣ — it is never zero, so the stationary points come from cos x = sin x alone. Look for every solution of tan x = 1 between 0 and 2π.

omittedParts.reason: The student must sketch y = e⁻ˣ sin x on printed axes for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, showing the stationary points and intercepts. The engine cannot accept or mark a hand-drawn graph.

writtenQuestions.q:
Four Year 12 students want to organise a graduation party. All four students have the same probability, P(F), of being available next Friday. All four students have the same probability, P(S), of being available next Saturday.

It is given that P(F) = 3/10, P(S|F) = 1/3, and P(F|S) = 1/8.

Kim is one of the four students.

(a) Is Kim’s availability next Friday independent from his availability next Saturday? Justify your answer. (1 mark)

(b) Show that the probability that Kim is available next Saturday is 4/5. (2 marks)

(c) What is the probability that at least one of the four students is NOT available next Saturday? (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) No. If F and S were independent then P(S|F) would equal P(S). Here P(S|F) = 1/3, while P(S) = 4/5 (found in part (b)), and 1/3 ≠ 4/5, so the two events are not independent.

(b) P(F ∩ S) = P(S|F) × P(F) = (1/3)(3/10) = 1/10.
P(F|S) = P(F ∩ S)/P(S), so
1/8 = (1/10)/P(S)
P(S) = (1/10) × 8 = 8/10 = 4/5.

(c) P(a given student is available on Saturday) = 4/5, and the four students are independent of one another.
P(at least one NOT available) = 1 − P(all four available)
= 1 − (4/5)⁴
= 1 − 256/625
= 369/625
= 0.5904.

bandDescriptors.full: Not independent because P(S|F) ≠ P(S); P(S) = 4/5 shown from P(F ∩ S) = 1/10; and P(at least one not available) = 1 − (4/5)⁴ = 369/625.
bandDescriptors.partial: (b) correct but (c) computes P(all four unavailable) as (1/5)⁴ instead of using the complement of 'all four available'.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Start with P(F ∩ S) = P(S|F)P(F). That single value unlocks P(S) through the definition of P(F|S). For (c), 'at least one' almost always means 1 minus the probability of none.

writtenQuestions.q:
The curves y = e−2x and y = e−x − 1/4 intersect at exactly one point as shown in the diagram. The point of intersection has coordinates (ln 2, 1/4). (Do NOT prove this.)(a) Show that the area bounded by the two curves and the y-axis, as shaded in the diagram, is (1/4)ln 2 − 1/8. (3 marks)

(b) Find the values of k such that the curves y = e−2x and y = e−x + k intersect at two points. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Between x = 0 and x = ln 2 the upper curve is y = e⁻²ˣ and the lower is y = e⁻ˣ − 1/4.
Area = ∫₀^(ln 2) [e⁻²ˣ − e⁻ˣ + 1/4] dx
= [−½e⁻²ˣ + e⁻ˣ + x/4]₀^(ln 2)

At x = ln 2: e⁻ˣ = 1/2 and e⁻²ˣ = 1/4, giving
−½(1/4) + 1/2 + (ln 2)/4 = 3/8 + (ln 2)/4
At x = 0: −½ + 1 + 0 = 1/2

Area = 3/8 + (ln 2)/4 − 1/2 = (1/4)ln 2 − 1/8.

(b) Set the curves equal: e⁻²ˣ = e⁻ˣ + k.
Let u = e⁻ˣ, so u > 0, and every positive u corresponds to exactly one value of x.
u² = u + k
u² − u − k = 0

Two intersections means two distinct positive roots u.
Discriminant: 1 + 4k > 0, so k > −1/4.
Product of roots = −k > 0, so k < 0.
Sum of roots = 1 > 0, consistent.

So −1/4 < k < 0.

bandDescriptors.full: The area established as (1/4)ln 2 − 1/8, and −1/4 < k < 0 in (b) from requiring two distinct positive roots of u² − u − k = 0.
bandDescriptors.partial: (a) correct but (b) only applies the discriminant, giving k > −1/4 and missing the requirement that both roots be positive.
bandDescriptors.minimal: In (a) integrate (upper − lower) from 0 to ln 2. In (b) substitute u = e⁻ˣ to get a quadratic, and remember u must be positive for a real x to exist — the discriminant alone is not enough.

writtenQuestions.q:
The graph of a quadratic function represented by the equation h = t² − 8t + 12 is shown.(a) Find the values of t and h at the turning point of the graph. (2 marks)

(b) The graph shows h = 12 when t = 0.
What is the other value of t for which h = 12? (1 mark)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The turning point of h = t² − 8t + 12 lies midway between the zeros t = 2 and t = 6, so t = 4. (Equivalently, t = −b/(2a) = 8/2 = 4.)
h = 4² − 8(4) + 12 = 16 − 32 + 12 = −4.
The turning point is (4, −4), so t = 4 and h = −4.

(b) Set h = 12: t² − 8t + 12 = 12, so t² − 8t = 0 and t(t − 8) = 0.
That gives t = 0 or t = 8, so the other value is t = 8.

bandDescriptors.full: The turning point is t = 4, h = −4, and the other value giving h = 12 is t = 8.
bandDescriptors.partial: t = 4 is found but h is not evaluated, or part (b) is attempted without setting t² − 8t + 12 equal to 12.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The turning point sits halfway between the two zeros. For part (b), put h = 12 into the equation and solve t² − 8t = 0 by factorising, not by the quadratic formula.

writtenQuestions.q: Find the equation of the tangent to y = 5x³ − 2/x² − 9 at the point (1, −6). (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
Write the middle term with an index: y = 5x³ − 2x⁻² − 9.

Differentiate:
dy/dx = 15x² + 4x⁻³ = 15x² + 4/x³.

At x = 1: dy/dx = 15 + 4 = 19, so the tangent has gradient 19.

Use the point-gradient form through (1, −6):
y + 6 = 19(x − 1)
y = 19x − 19 − 6
y = 19x − 25.

bandDescriptors.full: The derivative is 15x² + 4/x³, the gradient at x = 1 is 19, and the tangent is y = 19x − 25.
bandDescriptors.partial: The derivative or the gradient 19 is correct but the equation of the line is not formed, or a sign slip turns 4x⁻³ into −4x⁻³.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Rewrite 2/x² as 2x⁻² before differentiating. Differentiating −2x⁻² gives +4x⁻³ — two negatives make a plus.

writtenQuestions.q:
The numbers 75, p, q, 2025 form a geometric sequence.

Find the values of p and q. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
In a geometric sequence each term is the previous one times the common ratio r.
The fourth term is the first term times r³:
75r³ = 2025
r³ = 27
r = 3.

So p = 75 × 3 = 225 and q = 225 × 3 = 675.

bandDescriptors.full: The common ratio is 3, giving p = 225 and q = 675.
bandDescriptors.partial: r = 3 is found but p and q are not both stated, or the sequence is treated as arithmetic and a common difference is used instead.
bandDescriptors.minimal: There are three steps from 75 to 2025, so r³ = 2025 ÷ 75 = 27, not r = 27.

writtenQuestions.q:
In a research study, participants were asked to record the number of minutes they spent watching television and the number of minutes they spent exercising each day over a period of 3 months. The averages for each participant were recorded and graphed.The equation of the least-squares regression line for this dataset is y = 64.3 − 0.7x.

(a) Describe the bivariate dataset in terms of its form and direction. (2 marks)

(b) Interpret the values of the slope and y-intercept of the regression line in the context of this dataset. (2 marks)

(c) Jo spends an average of 42 minutes per day watching television.
Use the equation of the regression line to determine how many minutes on average Jo is expected to exercise each day. (1 mark)

(d) Explain why it is NOT appropriate to extrapolate the regression line to predict the average number of minutes of exercise per day for someone who watches an average of 2 hours of television per day. (1 mark)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Form: linear. Direction: negative.

(b) The slope −0.7 means that for each extra minute per day spent watching television, the average time spent exercising falls by about 0.7 minutes.
The y-intercept 64.3 means a participant who watches no television is predicted to exercise about 64.3 minutes per day.

(c) y = 64.3 − 0.7 × 42 = 64.3 − 29.4 = 34.9 minutes.

(d) 2 hours is 120 minutes, which is well outside the range of the data (0 to about 60 minutes). The linear relationship has not been shown to hold beyond that range, so a prediction there is unreliable.

bandDescriptors.full: Linear and negative; the slope is a fall of 0.7 exercise minutes per extra television minute and the intercept is 64.3 minutes at zero television; Jo is predicted 34.9 minutes; and 120 minutes lies outside the data range of 0–60.
bandDescriptors.partial: Some parts are right but the slope or intercept is stated as a bare number without being tied to minutes of television and exercise, or the extrapolation answer says only that 120 is 'too big'.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Interpreting a slope means saying what one extra unit of x does to y, in the units of the question. The extrapolation argument must name the range of the data.

writtenQuestions.q:
A sound wave can be modelled using a function P(t) = k sin at, where P is air pressure in Pascals, t is time in milliseconds (ms) and k and a are constants.

(a) Write the equation for a sound wave P1(t) that has an amplitude of 2 Pascals and a period of 5 ms. (2 marks)

(c) Hence, find the values of t, where 0 < t < 10, for which functions P1(t) and P2(t) = 4 sin(πt/10) are BOTH decreasing. (2 marks)

Part (b), which asked for the graph of P2(t) = 4 sin(πt/10) to be sketched on a printed diagram, is not included here. Its definition of P2 has been repeated in part (c) above, which is otherwise NESA’s wording and is answerable from the two equations alone.
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The amplitude is k, so k = 2.
The period of k sin at is 2π/a, so 2π/a = 5 and a = 2π/5.
P₁(t) = 2 sin(2πt/5).

(c) A sine curve decreases on the part of its cycle from the maximum to the minimum.

P₁ has period 5, with a maximum at t = 1.25 and a minimum at t = 3.75, so it is decreasing for 1.25 < t < 3.75 and again for 6.25 < t < 8.75.

P₂ has period 2π ÷ (π/10) = 20, with a maximum at t = 5 and a minimum at t = 15, so on 0 < t < 10 it is decreasing for 5 < t < 10.

Both are decreasing on the overlap: 6.25 < t < 8.75.

bandDescriptors.full: P₁(t) = 2 sin(2πt/5), and both functions are decreasing for 6.25 < t < 8.75.
bandDescriptors.partial: The equation in part (a) is correct but the overlap is not found, or only one of the two decreasing intervals of P₁ is considered.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Amplitude gives k directly; the period gives a through period = 2π/a. For the second part, find where each curve falls and take the values of t common to both.

omittedParts.reason: The student must sketch the graph of P₂(t) = 4 sin(πt/10) on a printed diagram that already carries the graph of P₁(t). The engine cannot accept or mark a hand-drawn graph.

writtenQuestions.q:
Consider the function f(x) = x²/ex.

(a) Find the stationary points of the function and determine their nature. (4 marks)

Part (b), which asked for a partially completed printed graph of f(x) to be completed, is not included here.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Write f(x) = x²e⁻ˣ and differentiate with the product rule:
f′(x) = 2xe⁻ˣ − x²e⁻ˣ = e⁻ˣ x(2 − x).

e⁻ˣ is never zero, so f′(x) = 0 when x = 0 or x = 2.

f(0) = 0 and f(2) = 4/e² ≈ 0.54, so the stationary points are (0, 0) and (2, 4/e²).

Test the sign of f′ = e⁻ˣ x(2 − x), whose sign is the sign of x(2 − x):
x < 0: negative;  0 < x < 2: positive;  x > 2: negative.

So (0, 0) is a minimum turning point and (2, 4/e²) is a maximum turning point.

bandDescriptors.full: f′(x) = e⁻ˣx(2 − x), giving a minimum at (0, 0) and a maximum at (2, 4/e²), with the nature justified.
bandDescriptors.partial: Both stationary points are found but their nature is not tested, or only one of the two is found.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Use the product rule on x²e⁻ˣ, then factor out e⁻ˣ — it is always positive, so the sign of f′ is decided by x(2 − x) alone.

Interest is charged at 0.5% monthly, compounded monthly.

On the last day of each month, interest is added to the balance owing on the loan and then the monthly repayment of $5740 is made.

Let $An be the balance owing on the loan at the end of n months.

(a) Show that A2 = 800 000(1.005)² − 5740(1.005) − 5740. (2 marks)

(b) Show that An = 1 148 000 − 348 000(1.005)n. (3 marks)

(c) After how many months will the balance owing on the loan first be less than $400 000? (2 marks)

bandDescriptors.full: A₂ is built by applying interest then a repayment twice, the geometric series is summed to give Aₙ = 1 148 000 − 348 000(1.005)ⁿ, and solving Aₙ < 400 000 gives 154 months.
