writtenQuestions.q: Find the range of g(f(x)), given f(x) = 3/(x − 1) and g(x) = x + 5. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
g(f(x)) = f(x) + 5 = 3/(x − 1) + 5.

The fraction 3/(x − 1) can take any real value except 0 (a fraction with a non-zero numerator is never zero).

Adding 5 shifts every value up by 5, so g(f(x)) takes every real value except 5.

Range: y ≠ 5, that is (−∞, 5) ∪ (5, ∞).

bandDescriptors.full: g(f(x)) = 3/(x − 1) + 5, so the range is all real numbers except 5.
bandDescriptors.partial: The composite is formed correctly but the range is given as all real numbers, or the excluded value is given as 0 rather than 5.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Substitute f into g, not g into f. Then ask which values the expression can never take: 3/(x − 1) is never 0, so the sum is never 5.

The probability that the team wins when:

• Bala is selected is 0.4
• Cassie is selected is 0.2.

Given that the team wins, find the probability that Amara was selected. (3 marks)

writtenQuestions.q:
A continuous random variable X has a probability density function given by

f(x) =
{0   x < 1
1/x   1 ≤ x ≤ e
0   x > e


(a) Find the mode of the given probability density function. Justify your answer. (2 marks)

(b) Calculate the value of the 25th percentile (Q1) of this distribution. Give your answer correct to 3 decimal places. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The mode is the value of x at which f(x) is greatest.
On 1 ≤ x ≤ e, f(x) = 1/x is a decreasing function, so its largest value occurs at the left endpoint x = 1, where f(1) = 1.
The mode is x = 1.

(b) The 25th percentile q satisfies ∫₁^q (1/x) dx = 0.25.
[ln x]₁^q = ln q − ln 1 = ln q.
ln q = 0.25
q = e^0.25 ≈ 1.2840254.

Q₁ ≈ 1.284.

bandDescriptors.full: The mode is x = 1 because 1/x is decreasing on [1, e], and Q₁ = e^0.25 ≈ 1.284.
bandDescriptors.partial: The mode is stated without justification, or the integral is set up correctly but not solved for q, or the answer is not given to 3 decimal places.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The mode of a continuous distribution is where the density is highest, not where the area is half. For the quartile, integrate the density from 1 up to q and set the area equal to 0.25.

writtenQuestions.q: Prove that (sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ)/(sin²θ cos²θ) + 2 = sec²θ cosec²θ. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
Start with the left-hand side and put the 2 over the common denominator:

LHS = (sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ)/(sin²θ cos²θ) + 2
    = (sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ + 2sin²θ cos²θ)/(sin²θ cos²θ).

The numerator is a perfect square:
sin⁴θ + 2sin²θ cos²θ + cos⁴θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)² = 1² = 1.

So LHS = 1/(sin²θ cos²θ) = (1/cos²θ)(1/sin²θ) = sec²θ cosec²θ = RHS.

bandDescriptors.full: The 2 is written over the common denominator, the numerator is recognised as (sin²θ + cos²θ)² = 1, and the result reduces to sec²θ cosec²θ.
bandDescriptors.partial: The common denominator is formed but the perfect square is not recognised, or the proof starts from both sides at once without connecting them.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Multiply the 2 by sin²θcos²θ/sin²θcos²θ so everything sits over one denominator. The numerator is then a perfect square of the Pythagorean identity.

writtenQuestions.q:
(a) In a flock of 12 600 sheep, the ratio of males to females is 1 : 20.

The weights of the male sheep are normally distributed with a mean of 76.2 kg and a standard deviation of 6.8 kg.

In the flock, 15 of the male sheep each weigh more than x kg.

Find the value of x. (4 marks)

(b) The weights of the female sheep are also normally distributed but have a smaller mean and smaller standard deviation than the weights of male sheep.

Explain whether it could be expected that 300 of the females from the flock each weigh more than x kg, where x is the value found in part (a). (1 mark)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The ratio 1 : 20 splits the flock into 21 parts, so the number of males is 12 600 ÷ 21 = 600 (and there are 12 000 females).

The proportion of males above x kg is 15/600 = 0.025, that is 2.5%.

For a normal distribution, 95% of values lie within two standard deviations of the mean, so 2.5% lie above μ + 2σ.

x = 76.2 + 2(6.8) = 76.2 + 13.6 = 89.8 kg.

(b) 300 out of 12 000 females is also 2.5%. But the females have a smaller mean and a smaller standard deviation, so 89.8 kg is more than two standard deviations above the female mean. The proportion of females above 89.8 kg is therefore well under 2.5%, and far fewer than 300 would be expected.

bandDescriptors.full: There are 600 males, 15 of them is 2.5%, which is two standard deviations above the mean, so x = 89.8 kg; and fewer than 300 females would be expected because 89.8 kg is more than two female standard deviations above a smaller female mean.
bandDescriptors.partial: x = 89.8 is found but part (b) is answered as 'yes, also 2.5%', or the flock is split as 12 600 ÷ 20 rather than ÷ 21.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The ratio 1 : 20 means 21 equal parts, not 20. Then turn 15 out of the male total into a percentage and match it to the empirical rule.

writtenQuestions.q: The graphs of y = e ln x and y = ax² + c are shown. The line y = x is a tangent to both graphs at their point of intersection.Find the values of a and c. (4 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
The line y = x has gradient 1, so both curves have gradient 1 at the point of contact.

For y = e ln x: dy/dx = e/x. Setting e/x = 1 gives x = e.
Then y = e ln e = e, so the point of contact is (e, e). It lies on y = x, as expected.

For y = ax² + c: dy/dx = 2ax. At x = e this must equal 1:
2ae = 1, so a = 1/(2e).

The parabola also passes through (e, e):
a e² + c = e
e²/(2e) + c = e
e/2 + c = e
c = e/2.

So a = 1/(2e) and c = e/2.

bandDescriptors.full: The point of contact is (e, e), found from e/x = 1; then 2ae = 1 gives a = 1/(2e) and substituting the point gives c = e/2.
bandDescriptors.partial: The point of contact is found but only one of a and c follows, or the gradient condition is used without also substituting the point into the parabola.
bandDescriptors.minimal: A common tangent of gradient 1 means each curve has derivative 1 there. Find the x-value from the logarithmic curve first, since it fixes the point.

writtenQuestions.q:
(a) Show that d/dx (sin x − x cos x) = x sin x. (2 marks)

(b) Hence, find the value of ∫02025π x sin x dx. (2 marks)

(c) The regions bounded by the x-axis and the graph of y = x sin x for x ≥ 0 are shown.Let An = ∫(n−1)πnπ x sin x dx, where n is a positive integer.

It can be shown that |An| = (2n − 1)π. (Do NOT prove this.)

Find the exact total area of the regions bounded by the curve y = x sin x and the x-axis between x = 0 and x = 2025π. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Differentiate term by term, using the product rule on x cos x:
d/dx (sin x) = cos x
d/dx (x cos x) = cos x − x sin x
So d/dx (sin x − x cos x) = cos x − (cos x − x sin x) = x sin x.

(b) Part (a) makes sin x − x cos x a primitive of x sin x:
∫₀^2025π x sin x dx = [sin x − x cos x]₀^2025π
= (sin 2025π − 2025π cos 2025π) − (sin 0 − 0)
2025 is odd, so cos 2025π = −1 and sin 2025π = 0.
= 0 − 2025π(−1) = 2025π.

(c) Area, unlike the integral, adds the size of every region:
Total area = Σ from n = 1 to 2025 of |Aₙ| = Σ (2n − 1)π.
The sum 1 + 3 + 5 + … + (2 × 2025 − 1) is the sum of the first 2025 odd numbers, which is 2025².
Total area = 2025²π = 4 100 625π square units.

bandDescriptors.full: The product rule gives the primitive, the definite integral evaluates to 2025π, and summing |Aₙ| = (2n − 1)π for n = 1 to 2025 gives a total area of 2025²π = 4 100 625π.
bandDescriptors.partial: Parts (a) and (b) are correct but part (c) reports the integral 2025π as the area, ignoring the regions below the axis.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The integral cancels regions below the axis; area does not. Sum the 2025 values of (2n − 1)π — the first n odd numbers add to n².

writtenQuestions.q:
A piece of wire is 100 cm long. Some of the wire is to be used to make a circle of radius r cm. The remainder of the wire is used to make an equilateral triangle of side length x cm.

(a) Show that the combined area of the circle and equilateral triangle is given by A(x) = ¼(√3x² + (100 − 3x)²/π). (2 marks)

(b) By considering the quadratic function in part (a), show that the maximum value of A(x) occurs when all the wire is used for the circle. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The triangle uses 3x cm of wire, so the circle uses 100 − 3x cm.
That is the circumference: 2πr = 100 − 3x, so r = (100 − 3x)/(2π).

Circle area = πr² = π(100 − 3x)²/(4π²) = (100 − 3x)²/(4π).
Equilateral triangle area = (√3/4)x².

A(x) = (√3/4)x² + (100 − 3x)²/(4π) = ¼(√3x² + (100 − 3x)²/π).

(b) A(x) is a quadratic in x. Expanding, the coefficient of x² is ¼(√3 + 9/π), which is positive, so the parabola is concave up and its vertex is a MINIMUM, not a maximum.

The maximum of a concave-up quadratic on a closed interval must therefore occur at an endpoint. The domain is 0 ≤ x ≤ 100/3, since the triangle cannot use more wire than there is.

A(0) = ¼ × 10000/π = 2500/π ≈ 795.8 cm² (all the wire in the circle)
A(100/3) = ¼ × √3 × (100/3)² = 2500√3/9 ≈ 481.1 cm² (all the wire in the triangle)

A(0) is the larger, so the maximum area occurs at x = 0, that is when all the wire is used for the circle.

bandDescriptors.full: The circumference gives r = (100 − 3x)/(2π) and hence A(x); the coefficient of x² is positive so the vertex is a minimum, and comparing the endpoints x = 0 and x = 100/3 shows the maximum is at x = 0.
bandDescriptors.partial: The expression in (a) is derived but (b) sets A′(x) = 0 and reports that stationary point as the maximum.
bandDescriptors.minimal: A concave-up parabola has its lowest point at the vertex, so the largest value on a closed domain is at one of the two ends. Test both.

writtenQuestions.q:
The shaded region is bounded by the graph y = (½)x, the coordinate axes and x = 2.(a) Use two applications of the trapezoidal rule to estimate the area of the shaded region. (2 marks)

(b) Show that the exact area of the shaded region is 3/(4 ln 2). (2 marks)

(c) Using your answers from part (a) and part (b), deduce e < 2√2. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Two applications over 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 use h = 1 and the three values x = 0, 1, 2:
y(0) = 1,  y(1) = ½,  y(2) = ¼.

Area ≈ (h/2)[y₀ + 2y₁ + y₂] = (1/2)[1 + 2(½) + ¼] = (1/2)(9/4) = 9/8.

(b) (½)ˣ = 2⁻ˣ, and ∫2⁻ˣ dx = −2⁻ˣ/ln 2.
Area = ∫₀² 2⁻ˣ dx = [−2⁻ˣ/ln 2]₀² = −(¼)/ln 2 + 1/ln 2 = (1 − ¼)/ln 2 = 3/(4 ln 2).

(c) The curve y = (½)ˣ is concave up, so each trapezium lies above the curve and the trapezoidal rule OVERESTIMATES the area:
9/8 > 3/(4 ln 2).
Multiply both sides by 4 ln 2 (positive):
(9/2) ln 2 > 3
ln 2 > 2/3
2 > e^(2/3)
Cube both sides: 8 > e², so e < √8 = 2√2.

bandDescriptors.full: The trapezoidal estimate is 9/8, the exact area is 3/(4 ln 2), and because the curve is concave up the estimate exceeds the exact value, which rearranges to ln 2 > 2/3 and hence e < 2√2.
bandDescriptors.partial: Parts (a) and (b) are correct but part (c) does not justify the direction of the inequality, or asserts the estimate is an underestimate.
bandDescriptors.minimal: For a concave-up curve the chords lie above it, so the trapezoidal rule gives too much area. That single inequality between (a) and (b) is the whole of part (c).

writtenQuestions.q:
A farmer wants to use a straight fence to divide a circular paddock of radius 10 metres into two segments. The smaller segment is ¼ of the paddock and is shaded in the diagram. The fence subtends an angle of θ radians at the centre of the circle as shown.(a) Show that θ = sin θ + π/2. (2 marks)

(b) The graph of y = sin θ + π/2 is shown.Use the graph and the result in part (a) to estimate the arc length of the smaller segment to the nearest metre. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Area of a segment = ½r²(θ − sin θ), and the whole circle has area πr².
The segment is ¼ of the paddock:
½r²(θ − sin θ) = ¼ πr²
Divide both sides by r² and multiply by 2:
θ − sin θ = π/2
θ = sin θ + π/2.

(b) The solution of θ = sin θ + π/2 is where the line y = θ meets the curve y = sin θ + π/2. Drawing y = θ on the given grid, the graphs cross at about θ = 2.3 radians.

Arc length = rθ = 10 × 2.3 = 23 metres (to the nearest metre).

bandDescriptors.full: Equating the segment area ½r²(θ − sin θ) to a quarter of πr² gives θ = sin θ + π/2; drawing y = θ on the grid gives θ ≈ 2.3, so the arc length is 10θ ≈ 23 m.
bandDescriptors.partial: The equation in (a) is derived but (b) uses the chord length instead of the arc, or reads a value of θ without drawing the line y = θ.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The r² cancels in part (a), which is why the radius never appears. In part (b) the equation θ = sin θ + π/2 says the line y = θ crosses the printed curve — draw it and read off θ, then use arc = rθ.

writtenQuestions.q:
The point T is the peak of a mountain and the point O is directly below the mountain’s peak. The point Y is due east of O and the angle of elevation of T from Y is 60°. The point F is 4 km south-west of Y. The points O, Y and F are on level ground. The angle of elevation of T from F is 45°.(a) Let the height of the mountain be h.
Show that OY = h/√3. (1 mark)

(b) Hence, or otherwise, find the value of h, correct to 2 decimal places. (3 marks)

(c) Find the bearing of point O from point F, correct to the nearest degree. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Triangle TOY is right-angled at O, with the angle of elevation 60° at Y.
tan 60° = h/OY, so OY = h/tan 60° = h/√3.

(b) From F the elevation is 45°, so OF = h/tan 45° = h.

Set up coordinates on the level ground with O at the origin, east as x and north as y.
Y is due east: Y = (h/√3, 0).
F is 4 km south-west of Y, so F = (h/√3 − 4/√2, −4/√2) = (h/√3 − 2√2, −2√2).

OF² = h² gives
(h/√3 − 2√2)² + (2√2)² = h²
h²/3 − (4√6/3)h + 8 + 8 = h²
Multiply by 3: h² − 4√6 h + 48 = 3h²
2h² + 4√6 h − 48 = 0
h² + 2√6 h − 24 = 0
h = (−2√6 + √(24 + 96))/2 = −√6 + √30 ≈ 3.03.

h ≈ 3.03 km.

(c) With h = 3.0277, OY = h/√3 = 1.7481, so
F = (1.7481 − 2.8284, −2.8284) = (−1.0804, −2.8284).

From F, the point O lies 1.0804 km east and 2.8284 km north.
The angle east of north is arctan(1.0804/2.8284) = arctan(0.3820) = 20.9°.

The bearing of O from F is 021° (to the nearest degree).

bandDescriptors.full: OY = h/√3 and OF = h; resolving the 4 km south-west step gives h² + 2√6h − 24 = 0 and h ≈ 3.03 km, and the bearing of O from F is about 021°.
bandDescriptors.partial: Part (a) and OF = h are correct but the south-west displacement is not resolved into east and north components, or the bearing is measured from the wrong end (the bearing of F from O rather than O from F).
bandDescriptors.minimal: South-west is 4/√2 km west and 4/√2 km south. Put O at the origin, write F's coordinates, and use OF = h. A bearing is measured clockwise from north at the point you are standing on — here that is F.

writtenQuestions.q:
The parabola with equation y = (x − 1)(x − 5) is translated both horizontally to the right and vertically up by k units, where k is positive.

The translated parabola passes through the point (6, 11).

Find the value of k. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
Translating right by k replaces x with x − k; translating up by k adds k:
y = (x − k − 1)(x − k − 5) + k.

Substitute the point (6, 11):
11 = (6 − k − 1)(6 − k − 5) + k
11 = (5 − k)(1 − k) + k
11 = 5 − 5k − k + k² + k
11 = k² − 5k + 5
k² − 5k − 6 = 0
(k − 6)(k + 1) = 0
k = 6 or k = −1.

k is positive, so k = 6.

bandDescriptors.full: The translated parabola is y = (x − k − 1)(x − k − 5) + k; substituting (6, 11) gives k² − 5k − 6 = 0 and, since k > 0, k = 6.
bandDescriptors.partial: The quadratic in k is formed but both roots are given, or the horizontal translation is applied as x + k instead of x − k.
bandDescriptors.minimal: A shift to the RIGHT by k replaces every x with x − k. Substitute the point and solve the resulting quadratic, then discard the negative root.

writtenQuestions.q:
The equation cos px = ½ has 2 solutions where 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π and p > 0.

Find all possible values of p. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
Let u = px. As x runs over 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π and p > 0, u runs over 0 ≤ u ≤ 2πp.

cos u = ½ has solutions u = π/3, 5π/3, 7π/3, 11π/3, … (that is π/3 + 2kπ and 5π/3 + 2kπ).

There are exactly 2 solutions when the upper limit 2πp reaches the second solution but not the third:
5π/3 ≤ 2πp < 7π/3.

Divide through by 2π:
5/6 ≤ p < 7/6.

bandDescriptors.full: Substituting u = px stretches the domain to 0 ≤ u ≤ 2πp; the solutions of cos u = ½ are π/3, 5π/3, 7π/3, …, so exactly two are captured when 5/6 ≤ p < 7/6.
bandDescriptors.partial: The list of solutions of cos u = ½ is correct but the endpoints are both made strict or both inclusive, or only p ≥ 5/6 is given with no upper bound.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Rewrite the domain in terms of u = px. The endpoint 5π/3 must be reached (so ≤) but 7π/3 must not be (so <) — the two inequalities are not the same kind.

writtenQuestions.q:
The graph of the function g(x) is shown.Using the graph, complete the table with the words positive, zero or negative as appropriate.
x-valueFirst derivative of g(x) at xSecond derivative of g(x) at x
x = −3  
x = 1  
x = 5
writtenQuestions.answer:
x = −3: first derivative positive, second derivative negative
x = 1: first derivative zero, second derivative zero
x = 5: first derivative positive, second derivative positive

Reasoning:
At x = −3 the curve is rising steeply towards the maximum near x = −2, so g′ > 0. It is bending over towards that maximum, so it is concave down and g″ < 0.

At x = 1 the curve is flat and tangent to the x-axis, and the concavity changes from up (on the left) to down (on the right). That is a horizontal point of inflection, so both g′ = 0 and g″ = 0.

At x = 5 the curve is rising steeply away from the minimum near x = 4, so g′ > 0, and it is concave up on that side of the minimum, so g″ > 0.

bandDescriptors.full: All six cells correct: (positive, negative), (zero, zero), (positive, positive).
bandDescriptors.partial: The first-derivative column is read correctly from the slope, but the concavity column is wrong at one or more values — most often calling x = 1 a stationary point without also recognising the inflection.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The first derivative is the slope of the curve; the second derivative is its concavity — positive where the curve is concave up, negative where it is concave down, and zero at a point of inflection.

writtenQuestions.q:
Find the sum of the terms in the arithmetic series

50 + 57 + 64 + ··· + 2024.
writtenQuestions.answer:
First term a = 50 and common difference d = 57 − 50 = 7.

Find how many terms there are, using Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d:
2024 = 50 + (n − 1)(7)
1974 = 7(n − 1)
n − 1 = 282
n = 283

Now use Sₙ = (n/2)(a + l), where l is the last term:
S₂₈₃ = (283/2)(50 + 2024)
    = (283/2)(2074)
    = 283 × 1037
    = 293 471

The sum of the series is 293 471.

bandDescriptors.full: d = 7, n = 283 and the sum 293 471.
bandDescriptors.partial: The common difference and the term formula are used correctly but n is out by one (282 or 284), or n = 283 is found and then the sum formula is misapplied.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Use Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d with Tₙ = 2024 to find how many terms there are, then Sₙ = (n/2)(a + l).

writtenQuestions.q:
The graph shows the populations of two different animals, W and K, in a conservation park over time. The y-axis is the size of the population and the x-axis is the number of years since 1985.

Population W is modelled by the equation y = A × (1.055)x.

Population K is modelled by the equation y = B × (0.97)x.Complete the table using the information provided.
Population WPopulation K
Population in 1985A = 34B =  
Percentage yearly change in the population  
Predicted population when x = 50 61
writtenQuestions.answer:
B = 280
Population W: 5.5% increase per year
Population K: 3% decrease per year
Population W when x = 50: 494

Reasoning:
B is the value of population K at x = 0, read from the graph as 280.

In y = A × (1.055)ˣ the base 1.055 = 1 + 0.055, so W grows by 5.5% each year.
In y = B × (0.97)ˣ the base 0.97 = 1 − 0.03, so K falls by 3% each year.

Population W at x = 50: y = 34 × (1.055)⁵⁰ = 34 × 14.5419… = 494.426…, which is 494 animals.

bandDescriptors.full: B = 280, W increases 5.5% per year, K decreases 3% per year, and W reaches 494 when x = 50.
bandDescriptors.partial: The two percentage changes are read correctly from the bases but B is misread from the graph, or 34 × (1.055)⁵⁰ is set up and then evaluated incorrectly.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The coefficient in front is the population at x = 0. In y = A × bˣ, a base above 1 is growth of (b − 1) × 100% per year and a base below 1 is decay.

writtenQuestions.q:
The curves y = (x − 1)² and y = 5 − x² intersect at two points, as shown in the diagram.(a) Find the x-coordinates of the points of intersection of the two curves. (1 mark)

(b) Find the area enclosed by the two curves. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Set the two expressions equal:
(x − 1)² = 5 − x²
x² − 2x + 1 = 5 − x²
2x² − 2x − 4 = 0
2(x − 2)(x + 1) = 0
x = −1 and x = 2

(b) Between x = −1 and x = 2 the curve y = 5 − x² lies above y = (x − 1)²:

Area = ∫₋₁² [(5 − x²) − (x − 1)²] dx
     = ∫₋₁² (5 − x² − x² + 2x − 1) dx
     = ∫₋₁² (−2x² + 2x + 4) dx
     = [−2x³/3 + x² + 4x]₋₁²
     = (−16/3 + 4 + 8) − (2/3 + 1 − 4)
     = (−16/3 + 12) − (2/3 − 3)
     = 20/3 − (−7/3)
     = 27/3
     = 9

The area enclosed by the two curves is 9 square units.

bandDescriptors.full: x = −1 and x = 2, and the enclosed area is 9 square units.
bandDescriptors.partial: The intersections are found correctly and the integral of the difference is set up, but the subtraction is the wrong way round or the primitive is evaluated incorrectly.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Equate the two expressions to find the limits, then integrate (upper curve − lower curve) between them. Over this interval the downward parabola is the upper curve.

writtenQuestions.q:
Initially there are 350 litres of water in a tank. Water starts flowing into the tank.

The rate of increase of the volume V of water in litres is given by dV/dt = 300 − 7.5t, where t is the time in hours.

Find the volume of water in the tank when dV/dt = 0.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Integrate the rate to get the volume:
V = ∫(300 − 7.5t) dt = 300t − 3.75t² + C

When t = 0, V = 350, so 350 = 0 − 0 + C, giving C = 350.
Therefore V = 300t − 3.75t² + 350.

Find when the rate is zero:
300 − 7.5t = 0
7.5t = 300
t = 40 hours

Substitute t = 40:
V = 300(40) − 3.75(40)² + 350
  = 12 000 − 6000 + 350
  = 6350

The tank holds 6350 litres when dV/dt = 0.

bandDescriptors.full: V = 300t − 3.75t² + 350, t = 40 and the volume 6350 litres.
bandDescriptors.partial: The rate is integrated correctly and t = 40 is found, but the constant of integration is omitted so the answer is 6000 litres, or an arithmetic slip is made in the substitution.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Integrate dV/dt to get V, and use the initial condition V = 350 at t = 0 to find the constant. Then solve dV/dt = 0 for t and substitute.

writtenQuestions.q:
Flowers were planted in two gardens (Garden A and Garden B).

On a particular day, 25 flowers were randomly selected from each garden and their heights measured in millimetres.

The data are represented in parallel box-plots.Compare the two datasets by examining the skewness of the distributions, and the measures of central tendency and spread.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Skewness: the dataset for Garden A is negatively skewed — its median sits towards the upper end of the box and the lower whisker is the longer one. The dataset for Garden B is positively skewed — its median sits towards the lower end of the box and the upper whisker is the longer one.

Central tendency: the median for Garden A (about 171 mm) is higher than the median for Garden B (about 152 mm), so the Garden A flowers are typically taller.

Spread: the interquartile range of Garden A (about 159 to 176 mm, so about 17 mm) is larger than the interquartile range of Garden B (about 149 to 158 mm, so about 9 mm). The range of Garden A (about 145 to 184 mm, so about 39 mm) is also larger than the range of Garden B (about 144 to 172 mm, so about 28 mm), so Garden A is more spread out on both measures.

bandDescriptors.full: Garden A negatively skewed and Garden B positively skewed, Garden A's median higher, and Garden A's IQR (or range) larger.
bandDescriptors.partial: Two of the three features are compared correctly — for example the medians and the spread — but the direction of the skew is reversed or not mentioned.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Compare three things: the skew (where the median sits inside the box and which whisker is longer), the medians, and the spread (interquartile range and range).

writtenQuestions.q:
In a particular electrical circuit, the voltage V (volts) across a capacitor is given by

V(t) = 6.5(1 − e−kt),

where k is a positive constant and t is the number of seconds after the circuit is switched on.

(b) When t = 1, the voltage across the capacitor is 2.6 volts.

Find the value of k, correct to 3 decimal places. (2 marks)

(c) Find the rate at which the voltage is increasing when t = 2, correct to 3 decimal places. (2 marks)

Part (a), which asked for a sketch of the graph of V(t) showing its behaviour as t increases, is not included here — the engine cannot mark a hand-drawn graph. Parts (b) and (c) work only from the equation above, so nothing from part (a) is needed. NESA’s wording of parts (b) and (c) is unchanged.
writtenQuestions.answer:
(b) Substitute t = 1 and V = 2.6:
2.6 = 6.5(1 − e^(−k))
2.6/6.5 = 1 − e^(−k)
0.4 = 1 − e^(−k)
e^(−k) = 0.6
−k = ln 0.6
k = −ln 0.6 = 0.510825…

k = 0.511 (3 decimal places)

(c) Differentiate: dV/dt = 6.5k e^(−kt).

When t = 2:
dV/dt = 6.5 × 0.510825… × e^(−2 × 0.510825…)
      = 3.32036… × e^(−1.02165…)
      = 3.32036… × 0.36
      = 1.19533…

The voltage is increasing at 1.195 volts per second (3 decimal places).

bandDescriptors.full: k = 0.511 and the rate 1.195 volts per second.
bandDescriptors.partial: e^(−k) = 0.6 is reached and k is found, but the derivative in (c) is wrong — most often the chain-rule factor k is dropped, or the unrounded value of k is not carried through.
bandDescriptors.minimal: In (b) isolate the exponential and take natural logarithms. In (c) differentiate V(t) = 6.5(1 − e^(−kt)), remembering that the derivative of e^(−kt) is −k e^(−kt), and substitute t = 2.

omittedParts.reason: The student must draw a sketch of the graph of V(t) = 6.5(1 − e^(−kt)), showing its behaviour as t increases. The engine cannot accept or mark a hand-drawn graph.

writtenQuestions.q:
In a game, the probability that a particular player scores a goal at each attempt is 0.15.

(a) What is the probability that this player does NOT score a goal in the first two attempts? (1 mark)

(b) Determine the least number of attempts that this player must make so that the probability of scoring at least one goal is greater than 0.8. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) P(misses one attempt) = 1 − 0.15 = 0.85
The attempts are independent, so
P(misses both attempts) = (0.85)² = 0.7225

(b) P(at least one goal in n attempts) = 1 − (0.85)ⁿ

Require 1 − (0.85)ⁿ > 0.8
(0.85)ⁿ < 0.2

Take natural logarithms. Because ln 0.85 is negative, the inequality reverses:
n ln 0.85 < ln 0.2
n > ln 0.2 / ln 0.85
n > (−1.60944)/(−0.162519)
n > 9.9032…

n must be a whole number, so the player needs 10 attempts.

bandDescriptors.full: P = 0.7225 in (a), and 10 attempts in (b) with the inequality (0.85)ⁿ < 0.2 solved by logarithms.
bandDescriptors.partial: (a) is correct and the inequality (0.85)ⁿ < 0.2 is set up, but the inequality sign is not reversed when dividing by the negative ln 0.85, or 9.9 is rounded down to 9.
bandDescriptors.minimal: 'At least one' is 1 − P(none). Set 1 − (0.85)ⁿ > 0.8, take logarithms of both sides, and remember that dividing by ln 0.85 (a negative number) reverses the inequality.

writtenQuestions.q:
A vertical tower TC is 40 metres high. The point A is due east of the base of the tower C. The angle of elevation to the top T of the tower from A is 35°. A second point B is on a different bearing from the tower as shown. The angle of elevation to the top of the tower from B is 30°. The points A and B are 100 metres apart.(a) Show that distance AC is 57.13 metres, correct to 2 decimal places. (1 mark)

(b) Find the bearing of B from C to the nearest degree. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) In the right-angled triangle TCA, the tower TC = 40 is opposite the angle of elevation at A and AC is adjacent:
tan 35° = 40/AC
AC = 40/tan 35° = 40/0.700207… = 57.1259…
AC = 57.13 metres (2 decimal places) ✓

(b) In the right-angled triangle TCB:
tan 30° = 40/BC
BC = 40/tan 30° = 40/0.577350… = 69.2820… = 69.28 metres

Now use the cosine rule in triangle ACB, where AB = 100:
cos ∠ACB = (AC² + BC² − AB²)/(2 × AC × BC)
        = (57.1259² + 69.2820² − 100²)/(2 × 57.1259 × 69.2820)
        = (3263.4 + 4800.0 − 10 000)/7915.0
        = −1936.6/7915.0
        = −0.24467…
∠ACB = 104.16…° = 104° (nearest degree)

A is due east of C, so the bearing of A from C is 090°. B lies a further 104° clockwise from CA, so
bearing of B from C = 090° + 104° = 194°.

The bearing of B from C is 194°.

A researcher is studying anacondas (a type of snake).

A dataset recording the age (in years) and length (in cm) of female and male anacondas is displayed on the graph.

Anacondas reach maturity at about 4 years of age.Write THREE observations about anacondas that may be made from the scatterplot. (Note: No calculations are required.)
writtenQuestions.answer:
Any three observations of this kind:

1. Female anacondas grow at a faster rate than males — the female points climb more steeply with age than the male points.

2. Both females and males continue to grow after 4 years of age, so growth does not stop at maturity.

3. Females are longer than males at any given age — at every age the female marker sits above the male marker.

(Other acceptable observations include: both sexes are about the same length at birth, near 75 to 90 cm at age 0; and length increases with age for both sexes.)

bandDescriptors.full: Three distinct, correct observations drawn from the scatterplot — for example that females grow faster, that both sexes keep growing after 4 years, and that females are longer than males at the same age.
bandDescriptors.partial: Two correct observations, or three statements of which one restates another rather than adding a new comparison.

writtenQuestions.q:
The graph of the function f(x) = ln(1 + x²) is shown.(a) Prove that f(x) is concave up for −1 < x < 1. (3 marks)

(b) A table of function values, correct to 4 decimal places, for some x values is provided.
x00.250.50.751
ln(1 + x²)00.06060.22310.44630.6931
Using the function values provided and the trapezoidal rule, estimate the shaded area in the diagram. (2 marks)

(c) Is the answer to part (b) an overestimate or underestimate? Give a reason for your answer. (1 mark)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) f(x) = ln(1 + x²)

First derivative, by the chain rule:
f′(x) = 2x/(1 + x²)

Second derivative, by the quotient rule:
f″(x) = [2(1 + x²) − 2x(2x)]/(1 + x²)²
      = (2 + 2x² − 4x²)/(1 + x²)²
      = 2(1 − x²)/(1 + x²)²

The denominator (1 + x²)² is always positive, so the sign of f″ is the sign of 2(1 − x²).
2(1 − x²) > 0 when x² < 1, that is when −1 < x < 1.

Therefore f″(x) > 0 for −1 < x < 1, so f(x) is concave up on that interval. ✓

(b) The shaded region is symmetric about the y-axis, so the total area is twice the area from x = 0 to x = 1.

Trapezoidal rule with h = 0.25 and five function values:
∫₀¹ f(x) dx ≈ (0.25/2)[0 + 2(0.0606 + 0.2231 + 0.4463) + 0.6931]
          = 0.125[2(0.7300) + 0.6931]
          = 0.125[1.4600 + 0.6931]
          = 0.125 × 2.1531
          = 0.2691375

Total shaded area ≈ 2 × 0.2691375 = 0.538275 square units.

(c) It is an overestimate.

From part (a) the curve is concave up on −1 < x < 1, so each trapezium's straight top edge lies above the curve. The trapezoidal rule therefore counts more area than there really is.

bandDescriptors.full: f″(x) = 2(1 − x²)/(1 + x²)² with the sign argument, the area 0.538275 (doubling the half from 0 to 1), and 'overestimate' justified by concavity.
bandDescriptors.partial: The second derivative is correct and the trapezoidal rule is applied correctly, but the symmetry is missed so the answer is 0.269 rather than 0.538; or (c) says overestimate with no reason.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Differentiate twice — chain rule then quotient rule — and argue from the sign of the numerator. For (b) note the shaded region is on both sides of the y-axis. For (c) a concave-up curve lies below its chords.

writtenQuestions.q:
A random variable is normally distributed with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. The table gives the probability that this random variable is less than z.
z0.60.70.80.91.01.11.21.31.4
Probability0.72570.75800.78810.81590.84130.86430.88490.90320.9192
The probability values given in the table for different values of z are represented by the shaded area in the following diagram.The scores in a university examination with a large number of candidates are normally distributed with mean 58 and standard deviation 15.

(a) By calculating a z-score, find the percentage of scores that are between 58 and 70. (2 marks)

(b) Explain why the percentage of scores between 46 and 70 is twice your answer to part (a). (1 mark)

(c) By using the values in the table above, find an approximate minimum score that a candidate would need to be placed in the top 10% of the candidates. (2 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) z = (x − μ)/σ = (70 − 58)/15 = 12/15 = 0.8

From the table, P(Z < 0.8) = 0.7881. This is the whole area to the left of z = 0.8, and 58 is the mean, so half the area (0.5) lies to the left of 58.

P(58 < X < 70) = 0.7881 − 0.5 = 0.2881

So 28.81% of scores lie between 58 and 70.

(b) The z-score of 46 is (46 − 58)/15 = −12/15 = −0.8, the exact negative of the z-score for 70.

A normal distribution is symmetric about its mean, so the area between 46 and 58 equals the area between 58 and 70. The interval from 46 to 70 is made up of those two equal pieces, so its percentage is twice the answer to part (a): 2 × 28.81% = 57.62%.

(c) To be in the top 10%, a candidate needs a score above the 90th percentile, so we need
P(Z < z) = 0.90.

The closest value in the table is 0.9032, at z = 1.3.

x = μ + zσ = 58 + 1.3 × 15 = 58 + 19.5 = 77.5

An approximate minimum score is 77 marks (accepting 78, since the score must exceed 77.5).

bandDescriptors.full: z = 0.8 giving 28.81% in (a), a symmetry argument using z = −0.8 in (b), and about 77 marks in (c) from z = 1.3.
bandDescriptors.partial: The z-score is correct but 0.7881 is quoted as the answer to (a) instead of subtracting 0.5; or (c) reads the table correctly and then fails to convert z back to a score.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The table gives the area to the LEFT of z, so subtract 0.5 to get the area between the mean and z. For (c), the top 10% starts where the left-hand area is 0.90, then reverse the z-score formula: x = μ + zσ.

writtenQuestions.q:
Jack intends to deposit $80 into a savings account on the first day of each month for 24 months. The interest rate during this time is 6% per annum, compounded monthly.

(a) Calculate how much money Jack will have in his account at the end of the 24 months. (3 marks)

(b) A table of future value interest factors could have been used to calculate how much money Jack would have in his account at the end of the 24 months.

Part of the table is shown.
Number of periodsInterest rate per period
 0.5% 
    
24 A 
    
What is the value of A in the table? Give your answer correct to 3 decimal places. (1 mark)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The monthly interest rate is 6%/12 = 0.5% = 0.005.

The first deposit is made on day 1 of month 1 and earns interest for all 24 months, so its future value is 80(1.005)²⁴. The next deposit earns interest for 23 months, and so on down to the last deposit, which earns interest for 1 month.

Total = 80(1.005)²⁴ + 80(1.005)²³ + … + 80(1.005)¹

This is a geometric series with first term a = 80(1.005), ratio r = 1.005 and n = 24 terms:
Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1)
   = 80(1.005) × [(1.005)²⁴ − 1]/(1.005 − 1)
   = 80.4 × (1.127159… − 1)/0.005
   = 80.4 × 25.4319…
   = 2044.73

Jack will have $2044.73 at the end of the 24 months.

(b) A future value interest factor is the future value of an annuity of $1, so the amount is 80 × A:
80A = 2044.73
A = 2044.73/80 = 25.5591…

A = 25.559 (3 decimal places).

bandDescriptors.full: $2044.73 in (a), from a geometric series with r = 1.005 over 24 deposits, and A = 25.559 in (b).
bandDescriptors.partial: The monthly rate 0.005 and the geometric series are set up correctly, but the number of interest periods is out by one — a common answer is $2034.56, from starting the first deposit at 23 months.
bandDescriptors.minimal: Convert 6% p.a. compounded monthly to 0.5% per month. Each deposit grows for a different number of months, so the total is a geometric series. In (b), the factor is the total per $1 deposited.

writtenQuestions.q:
A function f(x) is defined as

f(x) =
{0,   for x < 0
1 − x/h,   for 0 ≤ x ≤ h
0,   for x > h


where h is a constant.

(a) Find the value of h such that f(x) is a probability density function. (2 marks)

(c) Find the value of the median of the probability density function f(x). Give your answer correct to 3 decimal places. (2 marks)

Part (b), which asked the student to find a formula for the cumulative distribution function and sketch its graph, is not included here — the engine cannot mark a hand-drawn graph. Part (c) asks for the median of f(x) itself, so it needs only the value of h from part (a). NESA’s wording of parts (a) and (c) is unchanged.
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) A probability density function must enclose a total area of 1.

Between x = 0 and x = h the graph of y = 1 − x/h is a straight line from (0, 1) down to (h, 0), so the region under it is a triangle of base h and height 1:
½ × h × 1 = 1
h = 2

(Equivalently, ∫₀ʰ (1 − x/h) dx = [x − x²/(2h)]₀ʰ = h − h/2 = h/2 = 1, so h = 2.)

(c) With h = 2, f(x) = 1 − x/2 on 0 ≤ x ≤ 2. The median m satisfies ∫₀ᵐ f(x) dx = 0.5:

∫₀ᵐ (1 − x/2) dx = [x − x²/4]₀ᵐ = m − m²/4

m − m²/4 = 0.5
4m − m² = 2
m² − 4m + 2 = 0

m = [4 ± √(16 − 8)]/2 = [4 ± √8]/2 = 2 ± √2

The median must lie in 0 ≤ m ≤ 2, so m = 2 − √2 = 0.585786…

The median is 0.586 (3 decimal places).

bandDescriptors.full: h = 2 from a total area of 1, and the median 2 − √2 = 0.586.
bandDescriptors.partial: h = 2 is correct and the median equation m − m²/4 = 0.5 is set up, but the quadratic is solved incorrectly or the root 2 + √2 is chosen, which lies outside the domain.
bandDescriptors.minimal: For (a), the area under a probability density function is 1 — here the region is a triangle. For (c), the median splits the area in half, so solve ∫₀ᵐ f(x) dx = 0.5 and keep the root inside 0 ≤ m ≤ 2.

omittedParts.reason: The student must find a formula for the cumulative distribution function and then sketch its graph. The engine cannot accept or mark a hand-drawn graph.

writtenQuestions.q:
(a) Find the derivative of x² tan x. (2 marks)

(b) Hence, find ∫(x tan x + 1)² dx. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Use the product rule with u = x² and v = tan x:
d/dx (x² tan x) = x² sec²x + 2x tan x

(b) Expand the square first:
(x tan x + 1)² = x² tan²x + 2x tan x + 1

Now use the identity tan²x = sec²x − 1:
= x²(sec²x − 1) + 2x tan x + 1
= x² sec²x + 2x tan x − x² + 1

The first two terms are exactly the derivative found in part (a), so

∫(x tan x + 1)² dx = ∫(x² sec²x + 2x tan x) dx − ∫x² dx + ∫1 dx
                  = x² tan x − x³/3 + x + C

bandDescriptors.full: The derivative x² sec²x + 2x tan x, and the integral x² tan x − x³/3 + x + C.
bandDescriptors.partial: The product rule in (a) is correct and the square is expanded in (b), but tan²x is not rewritten as sec²x − 1, so part (a) cannot be used and the integral is left unfinished.
bandDescriptors.minimal: In (a) use the product rule; the derivative of tan x is sec²x. In (b) expand the bracket, replace tan²x with sec²x − 1, and look for part (a)'s expression inside the result.

writtenQuestions.q:
Anna is sitting in a carriage of a Ferris wheel which is revolving. The height, A(t), in metres above the ground of the top of her carriage is given by

A(t) = c − k cos(πt/24),

where t is the time in seconds after Anna’s carriage first reaches the bottom of its revolution and c and k are constants.The top of each carriage reaches a greatest height of 39 metres and a smallest height of 3 metres.

(a) Find the value of c and k. (2 marks)

(b) How many seconds does it take for one complete revolution of the Ferris wheel? (1 mark)

(c) Billie is in another carriage. The height, B(t), in metres above the ground of the top of her carriage is given by

B(t) = c − k cos((π/24)(t − 6)),

where c and k are as found in part (a).

During each revolution, there are two occasions when Anna’s and Billie’s carriages are at the same heights. At what two heights does this occur? Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places. (4 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) The cosine term oscillates between −1 and 1, so A(t) runs between c − k and c + k.

c + k = 39 and c − k = 3
Adding: 2c = 42, so c = 21.
Subtracting: 2k = 36, so k = 18.

(b) The period of cos(πt/24) is 2π ÷ (π/24) = 48.

One complete revolution takes 48 seconds.

(c) Set the two heights equal:
21 − 18cos(πt/24) = 21 − 18cos((π/24)(t − 6))
cos(πt/24) = cos((π/24)(t − 6))

Two angles have the same cosine when they are equal, or when one is the negative of the other (plus a multiple of 2π).

Case 1: πt/24 = (π/24)(t − 6) gives t = t − 6, which is impossible.

Case 2: πt/24 = −(π/24)(t − 6) + 2πn
t = −(t − 6) + 48n
2t = 6 + 48n
t = 3 + 24n

Within one revolution (0 ≤ t < 48) this gives t = 3 and t = 27.

When t = 3: A = 21 − 18cos(3π/24) = 21 − 18cos(π/8) = 21 − 18(0.923880) = 4.3702…
When t = 27: A = 21 − 18cos(27π/24) = 21 − 18(−0.923880) = 37.6298…

The two heights are 4.37 metres and 37.63 metres (2 decimal places).

bandDescriptors.full: c = 21, k = 18, a period of 48 seconds, and the two heights 4.37 m and 37.63 m at t = 3 and t = 27.
bandDescriptors.partial: (a) and (b) are correct and the equation cos(πt/24) = cos((π/24)(t − 6)) is formed, but only the t = 3 solution is found, so the second height is missing.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The greatest and smallest heights are c + k and c − k. The period of cos(πt/24) is 2π ÷ (π/24). For (c), equate the two heights and use the fact that cos θ = cos(−θ) — the second solution comes from adding a full 2π.

writtenQuestions.q:
Consider the curve y = ax² + bx + c, where a ≠ 0.

At a particular point, the tangent and normal to the curve are given by t(x) = 2x + 3 and n(x) = −(1/2)x − 2 respectively.

The curve has a minimum turning point at x = −4.

Find the values of a, b and c.
writtenQuestions.answer:
The tangent and the normal meet at the point of contact, so solve t(x) = n(x):
2x + 3 = −x/2 − 2
2x + x/2 = −5
5x/2 = −5
x = −2
y = 2(−2) + 3 = −1

So the point of contact is (−2, −1).

Differentiate the curve: y′ = 2ax + b.

At the minimum turning point x = −4 the gradient is 0:
2a(−4) + b = 0
−8a + b = 0, so b = 8a   … (1)

At x = −2 the gradient equals the tangent's gradient of 2:
2a(−2) + b = 2
−4a + b = 2   … (2)

Substitute (1) into (2):
−4a + 8a = 2
4a = 2
a = 1/2, and so b = 8(1/2) = 4.

The curve passes through (−2, −1):
(1/2)(−2)² + 4(−2) + c = −1
2 − 8 + c = −1
c = 5

So a = 1/2, b = 4 and c = 5.

bandDescriptors.full: The point of contact (−2, −1), then a = 1/2, b = 4 and c = 5.
bandDescriptors.partial: The two gradient conditions are set up correctly and a and b are found, but the point of contact is not obtained by intersecting the tangent and normal, so c cannot be determined.
bandDescriptors.minimal: The tangent and normal both pass through the point of contact, so solving t(x) = n(x) gives it. Then y′ = 2ax + b is 0 at x = −4 and equals 2 at the point of contact.

writtenQuestions.q:
Suppose the geometric series x + x² + x³ + ··· has a limiting sum, S.

By considering the graph y = −1 − 1/(x − 1), or otherwise, find the range of possible values of S.
writtenQuestions.answer:
The series is geometric with first term x and ratio x. A limiting sum exists only when |x| < 1, that is −1 < x < 1, and (since a first term of 0 is not a series of this kind we may also note x = 0 gives S = 0, which is inside the range found below).

S = a/(1 − r) = x/(1 − x)

Rewrite this in the form given:
−1 − 1/(x − 1) = [−(x − 1) − 1]/(x − 1) = (−x + 1 − 1)/(x − 1) = −x/(x − 1) = x/(1 − x)

So S = −1 − 1/(x − 1), which is the graph of y = −1/x shifted 1 unit right and 1 unit down: a hyperbola with vertical asymptote x = 1 and horizontal asymptote y = −1.

Its derivative is dy/dx = 1/(x − 1)², which is positive everywhere it is defined, so the function is increasing on (−∞, 1).

Now read off the branch on −1 < x < 1:
At x = −1: y = −1 − 1/(−2) = −1 + 1/2 = −1/2 (not attained, since x = −1 is excluded).
As x → 1⁻: x − 1 → 0⁻, so −1/(x − 1) → +∞ and y → +∞.

Since the function is increasing across that interval, S takes every value above −1/2.

Therefore S > −1/2.

bandDescriptors.full: S = x/(1 − x) with the condition −1 < x < 1, the graph identified as a shifted hyperbola, and the conclusion S > −1/2.
bandDescriptors.partial: S = x/(1 − x) and the restriction −1 < x < 1 are both correct, but the range is read off the graph incorrectly — for example giving −1/2 < S < ∞ as a closed interval, or omitting the restriction and concluding all real S.
bandDescriptors.minimal: A geometric series has a limiting sum only when |r| < 1; here r = x, so −1 < x < 1. Show that x/(1 − x) is the same as −1 − 1/(x − 1), sketch that hyperbola, and read the y-values over −1 < x < 1.

writtenQuestions.q:
Two circles have the same centre O. The smaller circle has radius 1 cm, while the larger circle has radius (1 + x) cm. The circles enclose a region QRST, which is subtended by an angle θ at O, as shaded.

The area of QRST is A cm², where A is a constant and A > 0.Let P cm be the perimeter of QRST.

(a) By finding expressions for the area and perimeter of QRST, show that P(x) = 2x + 2A/x. (3 marks)

(b) Show that if the perimeter, P(x), is minimised, then θ must be less than 2. (3 marks)
writtenQuestions.answer:
(a) Area: QRST is the difference of two sectors of angle θ, radii 1 + x and 1:
A = ½θ(1 + x)² − ½θ(1)²
  = ½θ[(1 + x)² − 1]
  = ½θ(2x + x²)
  = ½θx(2 + x)          … (1)

Perimeter: the two arcs QR and TS have lengths θ(1 + x) and θ(1), and the two straight sides QT and RS each have length x:
P = θ(1 + x) + θ + 2x
  = θ(2 + x) + 2x

From (1), θ(2 + x) = 2A/x. Substituting:
P(x) = 2x + 2A/x   ✓

(b) Differentiate: P′(x) = 2 − 2A/x².

P′(x) = 0 when 2 = 2A/x², so x² = A and, since x > 0, x = √A.

P″(x) = 4A/x³, which is positive for x > 0, so this stationary point is a minimum.

Substitute x = √A into (1) to find θ:
θ = 2A/[x(2 + x)] = 2A/[√A(2 + √A)] = 2√A/(2 + √A)

Now compare with 2:
2√A/(2 + √A) < 2
⟺ 2√A < 2(2 + √A)          (valid because 2 + √A > 0)
⟺ 2√A < 4 + 2√A
⟺ 0 < 4, which is always true.

Therefore when P(x) is minimised, θ = 2√A/(2 + √A) < 2.   ✓

bandDescriptors.full: A = ½θ(2x + x²) and P = θ(2 + x) + 2x combined to give P(x) = 2x + 2A/x; then x = √A at the minimum, θ = 2√A/(2 + √A), and the comparison showing θ < 2.
bandDescriptors.partial: Part (a) is shown correctly and x = √A is found with the second-derivative test, but θ is not expressed in terms of A, so the inequality θ < 2 is asserted rather than proved.
bandDescriptors.minimal: QRST is the difference of two sectors, and its perimeter is two arcs plus two radial sides of length x each. In (b), minimise P, then substitute back into the area equation to get θ in terms of A and compare it with 2.
